techniques.name: Block-centric generation paradigm
techniques.algorithm_summary: Areas are primary, roads are the negative space between them. A planar mesh is built first; its cells are wards/districts, its edges carry roads and rivers. Explicitly contrasted by watabou with the road-centric (Parish & Muller) alternative.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The actual mesh construction: Voronoi seeding scheme, relaxation, and how the city footprint is clipped from it.

techniques.name: Underlying editable mesh (warp substrate)
techniques.algorithm_summary: One planar graph underlies everything; districts are faces, roads/rivers/walls are edge chains, wall towers sit on vertices. Warp mode overlays it and moves nodes; downstream geometry is re-derived, not dragged.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether re-derivation is full regeneration of cell interiors or an incremental offset update.

techniques.name: DCEL migration (0.7.0)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Whole project migrated to doubly-connected edge lists; named as the real reason for the 0.6->0.7 version bump. Gives O(1) face/edge/vertex adjacency, which is the prerequisite for growing districts across face adjacencies.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What it replaced (likely ad-hoc polygon lists) and which features it unblocked beyond districts.

techniques.name: Polygon offsetting / buffering for streets
techniques.algorithm_summary: Inward offset of cell polygons carves street ribbons as filled polygons (confirmed by SVG anchor points). Rewritten in 0.3.0 after naive offsets folded at reflex vertices, causing streets that 'suddenly narrow'.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether it uses a straight skeleton, Clipper-style boolean offset, or a hand-rolled variant; junction resolution rule.

techniques.name: Lot subdivision / triangular-building defect
techniques.algorithm_summary: Recursive bisection of ward polygons into lots. Original 'rather silly algorithm' produced sliver triangles; inferred fix is cutting perpendicular to the longest edge or OBB major axis, since watabou could reduce but never eliminate them. Resolved by 0.5.3.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The actual cut rule and stopping criterion; watabou's fix is only described in an uncaptured Reddit comment.

techniques.name: Largest-inscribed-rectangle building fitting
techniques.algorithm_summary: Take lot polygon, find the largest inscribed rectangle, reject if too small, cut it into sub-blocks, delete a random subset. Yields the L/U/T/cross/ring footprints seen in every map. Used for castles, temples, farms and houses.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The max-rectangle algorithm itself (watabou's 'doesn't work entirely correctly'), area threshold, grid size, deletion probability.

techniques.name: Shared courtyards
techniques.algorithm_summary: Density is reduced by deleting interior lots only (no street frontage) instead of random lots, producing enclosed voids. A placement constraint, not a new primitive. Highly recognisable visual signature.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The deletion rate and whether courtyards are merged when adjacent.

techniques.name: Coast generation (4-step)
techniques.algorithm_summary: 1) mark part of terrain as water before building; 2) build city normally, no wards in water ('bitten apple' shape); 3) delete the wall section bordering water; 4) assign seafront blocks as docks and draw piers.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the water region itself is chosen - watabou admits it lacks bays and peninsulas, so it is not a general noise field.

techniques.name: Adaptive coast LOD then abandonment
techniques.algorithm_summary: 0.4.3 made coastline fractal detail depth fall off with distance from city centre for performance. 0.5.5 abandoned fractal detail entirely for a smooth spline ('I should have done it long time ago').
techniques.biggest_unknown: The fractal refinement used before 0.5.5 and the LOD falloff function.

techniques.name: Rivers as mesh edge paths
techniques.algorithm_summary: River runs between patches along mesh edges like a road, then is smoothed and widened by offsetting. Explains constant width, inability to loop (a simple path has no cycle), bridge placement at street crossings, and the large generation-time cost.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Source/sink selection and the edge cost function; what changed in 0.6.0 to make the river 'more likely to run through the city'.

techniques.name: Ward types as hints + per-ward parameter sets
techniques.algorithm_summary: 10 ward types (Market, Merchant, Craftsmen, Temple, Administration, Docks, Slum, Patriciate, Gate, Castle, plus Military). Each ward carries layout parameters - alley grid regularity, building size, min size, variance - that drive its interior.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How types are assigned to cells, and the numeric parameter ranges.

techniques.name: Continuous option (parameter smoothing)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per-ward layout parameters were i.i.d., causing tiny buildings facing huge ones across one street. 'Continuous' blends parameters gradually across district borders - inferred as diffusion over the ward adjacency graph or sampling from a smooth 2D field. Shipped 0.4.3, removed 0.5.5.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether it was graph smoothing or a noise field, and the blend strength.

techniques.name: Ward reroll determinism contract
techniques.algorithm_summary: cmd+click regenerates one ward keeping type and shape. Implies ward interiors are a pure function of (polygon, type, params, seed) with no cross-ward coupling, and a hierarchical seeding scheme rather than one linear RNG stream.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The seed derivation function and the exact URL parameter vector.

techniques.name: Extramural spread and shanty towns
techniques.algorithm_summary: Outskirts first spawned only next to gates (0.3.0); shanty towns add many extramural wards (0.4.2); by 0.6.0 they 'spread along the coast, river and roads'. Produces the star/asterisk silhouette of ribbons hugging radial roads.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The sampling weight function - inferred as distance-field decay from roads/water and from the gate.

techniques.name: Farm fields
techniques.algorithm_summary: Random count of irregular convex patches tiling the outskirts with gaps, each filled with parallel hatch lines at a per-field angle (furrows). Inferred to reuse the same mesh+offset machinery as wards. Watabou admits they are 'drawn incorrectly'.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether fields are mesh cells or a separate subdivision; what watabou considers wrong about the drawing.

techniques.name: Neighbourhoods -> Districts
techniques.algorithm_summary: 0.5.3 neighbourhoods = connected components of same-type wards (union-find over adjacency), purely to reduce label count. 0.7.0 districts are grown from seeds at prominent city features with borders shaped by landscape, giving size-diverse, barrier-respecting regions.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The seed set and the growth cost function; inferred as multi-source flood fill / weighted Voronoi over the face adjacency graph.

techniques.name: Elevation gradient field
techniques.algorithm_summary: A synthetic height field, stronger around the castle and falling toward coast and river banks, whose gradient perturbs alley layout. Effect is subtle enough that users reported not seeing it.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The functional form and whether it biases alley direction, lot size, or both.

techniques.name: Street hierarchy (3 classes)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Main streets, regular streets and alleys, each a fixed width until 0.5.5 added variation. Main streets run plaza-to-gate; outside roads are splines drawn as thin double lines.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the main-street network is selected on the mesh (shortest path? betweenness?) and the actual widths.

techniques.name: Market placement + constraint relaxation policy
techniques.algorithm_summary: Market placement criterion is 'not adjacent to the central plaza', but violating layouts are accepted when nothing better exists, because discarding them 'will increase generation time'. Constraints are scored preferences, not hard rejections.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether other placements (castle, temple, docks) use the same accept-degraded policy.

techniques.name: Walls, towers and gates
techniques.algorithm_summary: Closed polyline of 8-14 segments around the outer ward ring; towers at vertices as squares or circles (selectable); gates are gaps where a main street crosses; buildings set back from the wall after 0.5.3. Gate generation reworked in 0.5.1, enabling 'More roads' (up to 6 gates on a small town).
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the wall polygon is derived from the mesh and how gate positions are chosen.

techniques.name: Isolines as coastline offsets
techniques.algorithm_summary: 3-5 nested curves parallel to the coastline in a lighter water tint, spacing widening with depth. Inferred as successive inward offsets of the coast polygon rather than contours of a depth field - explains the parallelism and the stated drawing cost.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The offset distances and whether river banks get the same treatment.

techniques.name: Curved district labels
techniques.algorithm_summary: Large uppercase letter-spaced sans-serif with the baseline warped along a curve fitted to the district, size graded by district area, some rotated near-vertical. Watabou states the techniques were 'invented from scratch' and describes none of them.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the label spine curve is fitted to a district polygon and how collisions are resolved.

techniques.name: Legend with numbered badges
techniques.algorithm_summary: Boxed corner list numbering the ward types 1-10, with dark filled circular badges carrying white numerals placed on each ward; the same number repeats on every ward of that type. Offered as the low-clutter alternative to labels.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Badge placement rule within irregular ward polygons.

techniques.name: Four-colour palette model
techniques.algorithm_summary: Exactly four colours - land, block fill, water, ink - definable by drag-and-dropping an SVG file. Watercolours overrides only the block colour per neighbourhood/district. All fills flat, no gradients or textures in the shipped style.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The exact SVG schema of the palette files (three examples exist online, uncaptured).

techniques.name: Dual rendering (screen + SVG)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every drawing operation is implemented twice, which watabou names as his largest standing maintenance cost and considered reducing to raw shapes. PNG export is capped at ~8MP. Argues for a single retained-mode scene with multiple back-ends.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing material - this is a design lesson rather than an algorithm.

techniques.name: Road-centric experiment (rejected)
techniques.algorithm_summary: A separate prototype loosely based on Parish & Muller 'Procedural Modeling of Cities' with the L-systems removed: roads grown organically like veins, terrain-adaptive, curvilinear or grid. Rejected on implementation cost, performance, and non-composability with block-centric features.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether any of it survived into MFCG's 'winding alleys', which shipped partially in 0.5.2 and was never explained.

techniques.name: 3D view as proportion instrument
techniques.algorithm_summary: Footprints extruded to prisms, flat-topped at first then pitched gable/hip roofs; a walking simulator was used to check sizes and proportions and directly caused quays to be widened. Toy Town shipped as a standalone visualiser.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How per-building height and roof type are chosen from the 2D footprint.

techniques.name: Name generators
techniques.algorithm_summary: City names mix English toponyms (Boridge Port, Crosperton, Stormwind) with heroic-fantasy compounds (Elmsword); district names use a simpler algorithm but are clearly conditioned on the seeding feature (CASTLE DISTRICT, WEAVER'S DOCKS, COBBLERS CROSSING).
techniques.biggest_unknown: The morpheme tables and the conditioning rule linking a district's seed feature to its name.

techniques.name: FMG interop
techniques.algorithm_summary: Azgaar's Fantasy Map Generator passes a settlement's size and location to MFCG, which builds a plan; MFCG's 'Overworld' button asks FMG for a surrounding world. Round trip is URL-parameter-based and lossy - users report roads and coastlines not tallying and a different world on return.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The exact parameter vector crossing the boundary.

techniques.name: Village Generator origin
techniques.algorithm_summary: Asked repeatedly for a village option in 2017, watabou replied that 'villages need their own separate generator, because they are quite different from towns/cities' - the documented origin of VG as a separate codebase rather than an MFCG size class.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing here; this slice predates VG's own devlogs.

top_insights: MFCG is block-centric: one planar mesh is built first, its faces become wards/districts and its edges carry roads, rivers and walls. Everything else - street carving, warping, river routing, district growing - is an operation on that one structure. Watabou states this explicitly and rejects the road-centric alternative on cost and performance grounds.

The coast algorithm is given verbatim in four steps (devlog 4923) and the building algorithm in five (devlog 11802: largest inscribed rectangle -> cut into sub-blocks -> discard some). These are the two most directly reimplementable passages in the whole slice.

Constraints are scored preferences that degrade to acceptance, never rejection-sampled, because generation time is a hard budget (a fraction of a second for a large city). Watabou says so directly about market placement.

Ward reroll (keep type and shape, re-randomise interior) forces ward interiors to be a pure function of polygon+type+params+seed, which implies hierarchical seeding rather than one RNG stream - a load-bearing architectural constraint for any reimplementation.

The visual identity is a strict four-colour flat-fill model (land, blocks, water, ink) with a three-tier line hierarchy, 45-degree hatching, towers on wall vertices, gates as gaps, piers as thin perpendicular bars, and street-inaccessible 'shared courtyards' as interior voids.

Two features were shipped and then deleted - Forests (0.3.0) and Continuous (0.5.5) - and almost every risky feature shipped default-off while imperfect. Watabou names an unfixed defect in nearly every post.

The two 'boring' releases are the important ones: 0.6.0's general refactor and 0.7.0's migration to a doubly-connected edge list, the latter being the stated prerequisite for organically grown districts.

Dual rendering (screen drawing + SVG drawing implemented twice) is repeatedly named as the largest maintenance tax; PNG export is capped at ~8MP. A reimplementation should use one retained-mode scene with multiple back-ends.
All 23 posts carry an identical scraped date; real dates were recovered by decoding 13 embedded Twitter snowflake IDs, anchoring the slice from Aug 2017 (0.4.3) to Feb 2019 (0.6.0).

techniques.name: getCityBlock per-edge street inset
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per patch edge choose half-width: wall 1.0, plaza frontage 1.0, artery 1.0, inner ordinary 0.5, outer-of-walls 0.3; then shrink() if convex else buffer(). Neighbour insets the matching half, so gaps equal MAIN_STREET 2.0 / REGULAR 1.0 / ALLEY 0.6.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Voronoi vertex ordering fixes edge/inset index alignment; artery test only checks vertex membership, not adjacency.

techniques.name: createAlleys recursive block subdivision
techniques.algorithm_summary: Cut perpendicular to the longest edge at ratio centred 0.5 with width 0.8*gridChaos; angle jitter +/-15deg*gridChaos, forced to 0 once piece < 4*minSq; leaf when square < minSq*2^(4*sizeChaos*(u-0.5)); leaf dropped with emptyProb; gap ALLEY 0.6 when splitting.
techniques.biggest_unknown: No depth/area guard: a degenerate cut (count!=2) can recurse forever.

techniques.name: Terraced-house alley-gap probability rule
techniques.algorithm_summary: Recursive call passes split = half.square > minSq/(u1*u2). P(alley)=1-t+t*ln t with t=minSq/square: 0.15 at 2x minSq, 0.40 at 4x, 0.67 at 10x, 0.94 at 100x. Big pieces get 0.6 alleys, house-sized pieces get gapless cuts = party walls.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Probability curve derived analytically, not Monte-Carlo checked.

techniques.name: createOrthoBuilding L/rect slicer
techniques.algorithm_summary: Freeze two orthogonal axes (longest-edge direction c1 and its rotate90 c2); recursively cut perpendicular-ish at ratio 0.4-0.6 with NO gap; leaf when square < minBlockSq*2^(normal()*2-1); keep leaf with prob fill; retry whole slicing while result empty. Dropped leaves among touching rectangles produce L/T/U footprints.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Same non-termination risk if cut degenerates; while(true) retry can spin at low fill.

techniques.name: filterOutskirts building-density falloff
techniques.algorithm_summary: Collect populated edges (arteries factor 1.0, city neighbours 1.0 if enclosed else 0.4); normalise each building's nearest-vertex perpendicular distance by that edge's max patch depth; divide by inverse-distance-weighted vertex density (gate=1, all-city vertex=2*rand, else 0); keep if Random.fuzzy(1) > result.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Code contradicts its own comment on density values; signed distance2line can yield negative dist = unconditional keep.

techniques.name: Cutter.bisect
techniques.algorithm_summary: p1 = lerp(v, next(v), ratio); cut direction = rotate90(edge rotated by angle); poly.cut(p1, p2, gap). angle 0 = exactly perpendicular, so rectangles stay rectangular.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None material.

techniques.name: Cutter.radial / semiRadial (Park wedges)
techniques.algorithm_summary: radial: triangle (centroid, v0, v1) per edge, shrink([gap/2,0,gap/2]). semiRadial: centre = existing vertex nearest centroid, skip edges touching it, inset a wedge side only when it is not already a polygon edge. Park picks radial when block.compactness >= 0.7 else semiRadial; gap = ALLEY 0.6.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None material.

techniques.name: Cutter.ring (Cathedral cloister)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Offset each edge inward by thickness, sort slices by edge length ascending (short sides first), peel iteratively keeping cut()[0] as the shrinking core and collecting halves[1] strips; return strips only, discard the core = hollow ring around a courtyard. Cathedral uses it 40% of the time, thickness 2 + 4u.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None material.

techniques.name: Polygon.shrink = sequential half-plane clipping
techniques.algorithm_summary: For each edge with d>0, clip the polygon against the inward-offset supporting line keeping cut()[0]. Always yields a convex result, honours per-edge distances exactly, changes vertex count, silently under-insets rather than failing when over-inset.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Depends on the cut() left/right return convention being reproduced exactly.

techniques.name: Polygon.buffer = offset + self-intersection resolution
techniques.algorithm_summary: Offset every edge independently into a 2n scratch ring, resolve self-intersections by inserting each intersection point twice (DELTA 1e-6 guards), walk the index ring into loops and keep the largest by area. Used for concave patches; reflex corners end up chamfered by the joint chord.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Exact artefact geometry at reflex corners and with mixed distances (author admits 'weird steps').

techniques.name: Polygon.cut half ordering convention
techniques.algorithm_summary: Intersect the infinite cut line with polygon edges; on exactly 2 hits build both halves and optionally peel each by gap/2. Hand-executed on a unit square: returns [half left of p1->p2, half right]. On count != 2 it silently returns the unchanged polygon.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Behaviour with >=3 intersections on concave inputs is a silent no-op that callers never check.

techniques.name: Ward zoning: WARDS deck + greedy rateLocation
techniques.algorithm_summary: Fixed 36-entry deck (21 Craftsmen, 5 Slum, 2 Market/Merchant/Patriciate, 1 Cathedral/Administration/Military/Park), 3 adjacent-pair swaps, shift() one per unassigned patch, Slum after exhaustion; each class's static rateLocation scores patches, lowest wins, +inf forbids.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Haxe statics are not inherited, so Craftsmen/Gate/Park/Farm/Castle resolve to null and are placed at random - reasoned, not executed.

techniques.name: Polygon.distance defect skews all distance-based zoning
techniques.algorithm_summary: distance(p) tracks the nearest vertex but never updates the return value, so it always returns the distance from vertex 0 despite its comment. Consumed by Administration/Cathedral/Merchant/Slum/Market rateLocation and the countryside cull, making zoning noisy by up to a patch diameter.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether MFCG's live look depends on the bug - reproducing vs fixing is a visual decision.

techniques.name: drawBuilding two-pass silhouette
techniques.algorithm_summary: Pass 1 strokes every block at thickness*2 with no fill; pass 2 fills every block with no stroke. The fill covers the inner half of the stroke (effective outline = thickness) and covers internal seams, so touching ortho blocks read as one outlined mass. Castle 0.6, Cathedral 0.3.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Multi-subpath fill rule matters only if blocks are allowed to overlap.

techniques.name: Road casing double-stroke
techniques.algorithm_summary: Same polyline stroked twice: 2.3 wide in palette.medium with CapsStyle.NONE, then 1.7 wide in palette.paper. Yields two 0.3 kerb lines around a 1.7 carriageway = 2.0 road matching the MAIN_STREET/2 insets of adjacent blocks. Roads are pre-smoothed by smoothVertexEq(3).
techniques.biggest_unknown: lineStyle passes false where alpha is expected; correct arg list has to be reconstructed.

techniques.name: Walls, towers and gates
techniques.algorithm_summary: Wall = closed polygon stroked 1.8 in dark. Tower = filled dark circle r=1.8 (citadel 2.7) at every non-gate wall vertex. Gate = 3.6-wide, 5.4-long dark bar drawn ALONG the wall direction (next - prev) with square caps, reading as a thickened gatehouse.
techniques.biggest_unknown: CurtainWall.segments is always true here; the water-broken-wall path is inert.

techniques.name: Palette: four-role colour system, 8 presets
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every draw call names only paper/light/medium/dark, so inverted palettes (BLUEPRINT, NIGHT) and flat ones (SIMPLE) work with no branching. All 8 palettes' hex values recorded in the findings file. Active = DEFAULT (0xccc5b8/0x99948a/0x67635c/0x1a1917), also the stage and window background.
techniques.biggest_unknown: No runtime palette switch in this snapshot (options UI absent per README).

techniques.name: CityMap layer order and streets as negative space
techniques.algorithm_summary: Back to front: one Shape per outside road, then one PatchView per patch (countryside not added), then all transparent hotAreas, then one Shape with city wall + citadel wall. model.streets are never stroked - inner streets exist only as the paper-coloured gaps left by getCityBlock.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Z-order among patches follows the centre-out patch sort; matters only for stroke overlap.

techniques.name: Shared Point identity as mesh topology
techniques.algorithm_summary: Adjacency is reference identity on shared Point objects (contains/findEdge/patchByVertex/Topology map). Vertices closer than 8.0 are merged by rewriting neighbours' references and mutating the shared Point in place; gate smoothing moves wall and both patches at once.
techniques.biggest_unknown: A value-type port needs an explicit shared-vertex or half-edge structure or walls/streets/blocks desynchronise.

techniques.name: Market fountain/statue furniture
techniques.algorithm_summary: No buildings at all. statue = bool(0.6) -> rect(1+u, 1+u) rotated to the longest patch edge; else circle(1+u) = 16-gon. offset = statue || bool(0.3), position = lerp(centroid, longest-edge midpoint, 0.2+0.4u). getCityBlock is never called, so the square is flush to the patch.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None material.

techniques.name: Castle bailey and reserved-vertex curtain wall
techniques.algorithm_summary: Block = patch.shape.shrinkEq(4.0) (flat MAIN_STREET*2 inset, not getCityBlock), keep = createOrthoBuilding(block, 4*sqrt(area), 0.6). Its own CurtainWall reserves every vertex shared with a non-city patch, excluding those from gate candidates and smoothing, so the castle gate faces the city.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Citadel validity gate (compactness < 0.75 throws and regenerates the whole city) interacts with Voronoi shapes outside this slice.

techniques.name: Generate-and-reject with whole-city restart
techniques.algorithm_summary: Model.build() runs in a do/try/catch loop; three throw sites (bad citadel shape, unable to build a street, bad walled area shape) discard the entire city and regenerate. Only local repair anywhere is createOrthoBuilding's retry loop. Stack overflows are not caught.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Expected restart rate per size is unmeasured.

techniques.name: MINSTD PRNG with fuzzy/normal helpers
techniques.algorithm_summary: Lehmer LCG g=48271, n=2147483647, seed0=1. float()=next()/n; normal()=(u+u+u)/3 (Irwin-Hall 3); int(min,max) exclusive of max; fuzzy(f)=(1-f)/2+f*normal(). Fully seed-reproducible except the city-size roll, which uses Math.random().
techniques.biggest_unknown: Any port must replicate the exact call ORDER, since every ward constructor consumes draws.

top_insights: Ward character is only four scalars - minSq, gridChaos, sizeChaos, emptyProb - fed to one recursive bisector; the whole MFCG ward vocabulary is that table plus rateLocation.
One line decides terraced vs detached housing: split = half.square > minSq/(u1*u2), so alleys are cut only while a piece is block-sized and house-sized cuts are gapless (party walls).
Angle jitter is switched OFF below 4*minSq ('keep buildings rectangular even in chaotic wards'), which is why slums have crooked blocks but straight houses.
Streets inside the walls are never drawn - they are the negative space left by getCityBlock's half-width insets; only outside roads are stroked, as a 2.3 medium casing over a 1.7 paper carriageway.
drawBuilding strokes all blocks at double width then fills them all, so createOrthoBuilding's touching rectangles read as one outlined L/T/U silhouette instead of separate boxes.

Polygon.distance() is broken - it returns the distance from vertex 0, not the nearest vertex - and it is the input to every distance-based rateLocation, so MFCG's zoning is far noisier than the comments imply.

Haxe does not inherit statics, so Craftsmen/Gate/Park/Farm/Castle have no rateLocation and are placed at random: ~22 of 36 ward slots are random, with only ~14 constrained placements creating the sense of zoning.

Every adjacency is Point reference identity on shared vertex objects, and the generator exploits in-place mutation of those shared Points (junction merge at 8.0 units, gate smoothing) - a value-type port breaks silently.

Validity is handled only by generate-and-reject at whole-city level (three throw sites) plus one retry loop in createOrthoBuilding; both recursive slicers have no depth guard and can hang on a degenerate cut.
Rendering is written entirely in four colour roles (paper/light/medium/dark), which is why inverted palettes like BLUEPRINT and NIGHT need no branching at all.
open_questions: Reproduce or fix Polygon.distance()? Fixing it makes zoning visibly tidier than MFCG's actual look.
Polygon winding (CCW, positive shoelace) and cut()'s [left, right] return order are never asserted in code - a port must pin them with tests or shrink/peel/ring keep the wrong halves.
Voronoi vertex ordering sets 'vertex 0' and the forEdge/insetDist index alignment; not recoverable from this slice (belongs to the Voronoi/core slice).

drawRoad and drawGate pass `false` where lineStyle expects alpha and CapsStyle where scaleMode goes - the intended argument list has to be reconstructed (recommend alpha=1, pixelHinting=false, caps=NONE).
Neither createAlleys nor createOrthoBuilding's slice() has a recursion guard; a re-implementer must choose a depth/area cap and what to emit when it trips.
filterOutskirts uses signed distance2line, so buildings on the outer side of an edge get negative normalised distance and are kept unconditionally - intentional or not is unknown.
Ward geometry is built once, globally, after all wards are assigned; an editable/incremental generator must define how getCityBlock is invalidated when arteries or walls change.

MFCG has no explicit street-frontage rule - frontage is emergent from cutting perpendicular to the longest edge. Whether an original generator should model frontage and per-ward orientation explicitly is the main open design question.
All constants are absolute world units, so a metropolis has the same house size as a small town with more of them; keep or abandon that scale invariance?

techniques.name: Bowyer-Watson incremental Delaunay with rectangular frame
techniques.algorithm_summary: Frame = 4 bbox corners + 2 triangles. Per insert: collect triangles whose circumcircle contains p (test dist(p,c)<r); cavity boundary edges are those whose REVERSE is not held by another cavity triangle (consistent CCW orientation); walk boundary via index=a.indexOf(b[index]) emitting Triangle(p,a,b); delete cavity. Circumcentre by perpendicular-bisector intersection using tg1=dy1/dx1. O(n^2) build.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None algorithmically; only whether modern MFCG still uses this core.

techniques.name: Voronoi dual extraction with frame-cell discard (partioning)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Region = triangles incident to a seed, sorted CCW by a half-plane + cross-product angular comparator (starts at bearing +90deg). Cell polygon = the triangles' circumcentre Points. partioning() emits only regions whose every triangle is 'real' (no frame corner), discarding all unbounded cells. Iterates points not the map so caller-visible ordering is preserved.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How many cells survive for a given nPatches (interacts with 25% frame margin).

techniques.name: Identity-shared mutable Point topology
techniques.algorithm_summary: No DCEL/index. Adjacency is reference equality of Point objects. Patch.fromRegion reuses the triangles' circumcentre Point instances, so neighbouring patches literally share vertex objects; mutating one moves the shared boundary everywhere at once (used for gate nudging and street smoothing). contains() is vertex membership, NOT point-in-polygon. Ops that replace rather than mutate Points (inset, cut, buffer, shrink, smoothVertexEq) sever topology, forcing a strict pipeline order.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing; but this is the one design I recommend NOT copying (use half-edge/vertex arena).

techniques.name: Spiral seed distribution with 8x oversampling
techniques.algorithm_summary: nPatches*8 seeds; angle a = sa + sqrt(i)*5 rad (sa a random global rotation), radius r = 0 for i=0 else 10 + i*(2+U(0,1)). Angular step shrinks as 2.5/sqrt(i) while radius grows linearly, giving dense regular centre and sparse organic rim. Points later sorted by |p| so region[0]=plaza, region[nPatches]=citadel.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether the 5-radian step (not the golden angle) is tuned or arbitrary.

techniques.name: Selective Lloyd relaxation (vertex-centroid)
techniques.algorithm_summary: 3 passes; each replaces selected seeds with Region.center() = mean of incident circumcentres (vertex centroid, not area centroid), then rebuilds the whole diagram. LATENT BUG: intended targets are the 3 central seeds but points[0..2] are the frame corners, whose regions partioning() always discards, so 3 of 4 relaxations are no-ops and the 4th drifts to a different seed each pass.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether to reproduce the bug or implement the stated intent (visibly more regular centre).

techniques.name: Polygon offsetting by self-intersection repair (buffer)
techniques.algorithm_summary: 1) push raw offset endpoints per edge with NO joint handling (author: 'may want something fancier for nicer joints'); 2) repeatedly find a proper crossing (both params in (1e-6, 1-1e-6)) and insert the SAME Point instance twice, at j+1 and i+1; 3) walk the loop treating duplicated Points as teleports (indexOf/lastIndexOf) to split into simple sub-loops; 4) return the sub-loop of greatest signed area. Handles concave input; up to O(n^3).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Intended joint style (miter vs round) — visibly changes block corners.

techniques.name: Half-plane intersection inset (shrink) + convexity dispatch
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per edge with d>0, build the inward-offset line (v1+n, v2+n), n = rotate90(edge).norm(d), and clip via cut(...)[0]. Result is always convex. Ward.getCityBlock dispatches: isConvex() ? shrink : buffer — the clearest statement of the two operators' trade-off. O(n^2).
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: Street width by per-edge half-width inset
techniques.algorithm_summary: Each patch edge is inset by half the width of whatever runs along it: wall-abutting or plaza/artery -> MAIN_STREET/2 = 1.0; inside walls -> REGULAR_STREET/2 = 0.5; outside walls -> ALLEY/2 = 0.3. Both abutting patches inset, jointly opening the full corridor. Units: regular street = 1.0.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None — most transferable recipe in the slice.

techniques.name: cut() line-clip with gap, and peel
techniques.algorithm_summary: Cuts along the INFINITE line through p1,p2; requires exactly 2 edge crossings else silently returns [self]. Halves get the crossing Points; if gap>0 each half is peel()ed by gap/2 along its new edge, carving a corridor of exactly gap. Return order verified by hand: result[0] is the half LEFT of directed p1->p2 — the contract shrink and peel silently depend on.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Left-half ordering verified on one worked case; assert with a property test.

techniques.name: Recursive perpendicular bisection for blocks/alleys
techniques.algorithm_summary: Cutter.bisect: pick a point at ratio along a chosen edge (Ward picks the longest), take the edge direction rotated by a chaos angle, cut perpendicular to it with gap = ALLEY. Ward.createAlleys recurses with area thresholds minSq*2^(4*sizeChaos*(U-0.5)), angleSpread = pi/6*gridChaos suppressed below 4*minSq, emptyProb default 0.04.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Full recursion parameters live in the wards slice, not this one.

techniques.name: Radial / semi-radial / ring subdivision
techniques.algorithm_summary: radial: fan triangles [centroid,v0,v1] per edge, shrink [gap/2,0,gap/2] to gap only the spokes. semiRadial: anchor on the polygon VERTEX nearest the centroid, skip degenerate sectors, use findEdge to skip gapping spokes that are real boundary edges. ring(thickness): offset each edge inward, sort edges SHORT-SIDES-FIRST, iteratively cut the shrinking core keeping halves[1] as ring strips.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Why short-sides-first (presumably sliver avoidance) is not stated.

techniques.name: Weighted Laplacian smoothing with pinned vertices
techniques.algorithm_summary: smoothVertex = (prev + f*v + next)/(2+f); f is the retention weight (f=1 = plain average, larger = gentler). smoothVertexEq applies it Jacobi-style to all vertices. Parameters: curtain wall f = min(1, 40/nWalledPatches) with reserved vertices pinned; gates get a second pass at f=1 applied in place via Point.set; streets f=3 with endpoints pinned (loop 1..len-1).
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: Compactness (Polsby-Popper) as a shape gate
techniques.algorithm_summary: 4*pi*A/P^2; code comments give circle 1.00, square 0.79, triangle 0.60 (exact: pi/4, pi*sqrt3/9). Used as a gate not a metric: Park picks radial vs semiRadial at >=0.7; citadel throws 'Bad citadel shape!' below 0.75; a farm/ward choice gates at >=0.7.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: Throw-and-regenerate failure strategy
techniques.algorithm_summary: Model.new wraps build() in do/try/catch/while(instance==null): any geometric degeneracy (NaN circumcentre, cut finding !=2 crossings, null path, bad wall shape) throws and the ENTIRE town is rebuilt, differing because the global PRNG has advanced. This is why the primitives are allowed to be fragile. Hazard: unbounded loop + URL-pinnable seed = deterministic infinite hang.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: Park-Miller MINSTD global PRNG with fuzzy/normal helpers
techniques.algorithm_summary: x <- 48271*x mod (2^31-1), multiply done in float so it is exact across targets. float() in (0,1); normal() = mean of 3 uniforms (Irwin-Hall n=3, mean 0.5, sigma 0.167); int(min,max) exclusive-max; fuzzy(f) = f==0 ? 0.5 : (1-f)/2 + f*normal(), a single dial from deterministic to full bell with the mean pinned. One global stream drives every decision, so any change in call order changes every map.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None. reset(0) is an absorbing state, guarded only by callers.

techniques.name: Pseudo-A* graph search (mis-named)
techniques.algorithm_summary: No heuristic and no priority queue: openSet.shift() pops in insertion order, and closedSet.push on pop means improved nodes are never reconsidered — so it is a best-effort BFS, NOT shortest-path. exclude pre-seeds the closed set (how roads are told to avoid regions). buildPath returns the path REVERSED. O(V^2). Sibling calculatePrice is broken (off-by-one -> NaN for len>=3) and unused.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether road quality depends on the non-optimality; replacing with real A* may change road shapes.

techniques.name: Shepard inverse-distance vertex interpolation
techniques.algorithm_summary: Polygon.interpolate(p): w_i = (1/dist(v_i,p)) normalised to sum 1 (power-1 Shepard). Used to blend a per-vertex density field (gates=1, all-urban vertices=2*U(0,1), else 0) at each building centre; buildings survive if Random.fuzzy(1) > minDist/p — the outskirts-thinning rule.
techniques.biggest_unknown: NaN if p coincides with a vertex (unreachable with floats).

techniques.name: Signed point-line distance for street frontage
techniques.algorithm_summary: distance2line's expanded numerator simplifies exactly to cross(d, p0-p1), so it is signed perpendicular distance cross/|d|, positive to the LEFT. Used to normalise each building's distance from its patch's 'populated edges' (edges on an artery weight 1.0, edges facing a non-enclosed urban neighbour weight 0.4).
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: Visvalingam-Whyatt decimation (simplyfy) - unused
techniques.algorithm_summary: Repeatedly remove the vertex with minimal |effective triangle area| of (prev,v,next) until n remain; recomputed from scratch each pass (no heap), O((len-n)*len). In-place. Zero callers in this release.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Why it exists — likely for a feature not in this snapshot.

techniques.name: Perlin noise (defective, unused)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Canonical 256-entry table, but seeded by ROTATION (only 256 correlated fields), indices unmasked (valid domain only ~[0,255]^2, breaks on negatives), quintic fade served from a 256-entry LUT (banding), gradients = hash&3 -> 4 unnormalised diagonals, gridSize ignored by noise(). noiseHigh carries the author's own comment 'INCORRECT! x & y should be updated as well' and returns identical octaves; only noiseMapHigh is a real fBm. Zero callers — matches README 'lacks waterbodies'.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Intended domain scaling / octaves / thresholding for water and terrain.

techniques.name: Catmull-Rom tangents to Bezier controls (Spline, unused)
techniques.algorithm_summary: curvature = 0.1 tension (vs canonical 1/6). Tangent at p1 ∝ p2-p0; midCurve emits [p1a, p12, p2a, p2] = two quadratics approximating one cubic split at the control-polygon midpoint (Flash-era workaround, Graphics has only curveTo). Driver curvePolygon is commented out; zero callers. Roads in this release are polylines smoothed by smoothVertexEq(3) and drawn twice (wide dark then narrow paper) for street casing.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether modern MFCG's curved roads use this scheme or a different one.

top_insights: LICENCE: full unmodified GPL-3.0, no additional permissions, no per-file headers. Copying or translating this code (a Haxe->TS port IS a derivative work) forces GPL-3 + source release. Techniques and maths are NOT protected, so the safe path is specification-by-observation: learn WHICH techniques and WHAT constants, then implement from independent standard references (Delaunator, Clipper2, Shewchuk predicates, PCG32). The numeric parameter tables are the most reusable output of this slice.

The whole layer is organised around ONE decision: topology is carried by reference-equality of shared mutable Point objects, because Patch polygons reuse the Delaunay triangles' circumcentre Point instances. That gives atomic shared-boundary moves (gates, streets) but costs O(n) adjacency, aliasing hazards and un-serialisable state. Ops that REPLACE Points (inset/cut/buffer/shrink/smoothVertexEq) sever it, which dictates the whole pipeline order. A rewrite should use a half-edge/DCEL or indexed vertex arena.

Streets are not drawn, they are CARVED: each patch edge is inset by HALF the width of whatever runs along it (wall/plaza/artery 1.0, inner 0.5, outer 0.3), both sides jointly opening the full corridor; cut(gap) + peel(gap/2) does the same for alleys during recursive bisection. Units: regular street = 1.0. This is the single most transferable recipe in the slice.

Three distinct inset operators with different contracts, and the code dispatches between two of them on shape: isConvex() ? shrink (half-plane intersection, exact, always convex) : buffer (raw offset + self-intersection repair + keep-largest-component, preserves concavity). inset() (per-edge slide, vertex-count preserving) is self-described unreliable and has zero callers.

CONFIRMED BUG that changes output: Polygon.distance() never updates its running minimum, so it always returns the distance from vertex[0]. It is the scoring function for Cathedral, MerchantWard, Slum, AdministrationWard and Market siting — so ward placement is scored from an arbitrary patch vertex. Fixing it moves wards on every seed; pin or fix deliberately.

LATENT BUG in relaxation: Model asks to Lloyd-relax voronoi.points[0..2] intending the three central seeds, but the Voronoi constructor puts the four frame corners at indices 0..3, and frame-corner regions are always discarded by partioning(). So three of four relaxations are no-ops and the fourth drifts to a different seed each pass. Implementing what the comment SAYS yields a visibly more regular city centre than MFCG has.

The global failure strategy is throw-and-regenerate-the-whole-town (Model.new's do/try/catch/while loop), which is precisely why the primitives are allowed to be numerically fragile. Hazard: the loop is unbounded and the seed is URL-pinnable, so a deterministically-failing seed hangs forever. A rewrite needs bounded retries with per-attempt re-seeding.

Seed distribution is a spiral, not Poisson-disc: angle = sqrt(i)*5 rad, radius ~ 10 + i*(2+U(0,1)), with 8x oversampling because partioning() discards every frame-touching cell. Angular step shrinks as radius grows, producing the signature dense-regular-centre / sparse-organic-rim gradient for free.

Spline and the entire PerlinNoise class have ZERO callers anywhere in Source/, confirming the README's 'lacks waterbodies': curved roads and terrain/water postdate this snapshot. Roads here are polylines smoothed by smoothVertexEq(3) and drawn twice (wide dark, then narrow paper) — the street-casing technique.

Primary numerical weakness to replace: the circumcentre uses tg1 = dy1/dx1, so a horizontal p1-p2 edge yields a NaN centre with no guard, and the in-circle test is a sqrt distance compare rather than an exact determinant. Random float seeds make exact ties improbable — which means ANY grid-aligned or snapped input in a rewrite breaks it immediately.

Graph.aStar is not A*: no heuristic, no priority queue (openSet.shift()), and closed nodes are never reconsidered, so it returns a valid but not-shortest path, reversed. Its exclude-set (how roads are told to avoid regions) is the idea worth keeping.

Reusable dials worth stealing outright: Random.fuzzy(f) (one parameter from deterministic 0.5 to full bell, mean pinned); compactness as a shape GATE at 0.7 / 0.75; pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing with f = min(1, 40/n); short-sides-first ordering in ring subdivision.
open_questions: Polygon.distance()'s bug alters ward siting on every seed — pin the buggy behaviour to match MFCG's look, or fix it? Must be decided deliberately and recorded.
Reproduce the frame-corner relaxation bug, or implement the stated intent (Lloyd-relax the three central seeds), which gives a visibly more regular city centre?

cut()[0] = the half left of the directed line p1->p2 was verified on one hand-worked case; shrink and peel silently depend on it, so a rewrite should assert it with a property test before building on it.

What the 8x seed oversampling is actually tuned to — it interacts with the 25% frame margin and partioning()'s discard rule, and the surviving-cell count is not obviously nPatches. Only instrumenting a real build will say.
Is the 5-radian angular step tuned, or arbitrary? It is not the golden angle, so whether the resulting near-resonances are part of the intended look is unrecoverable from source.
Intended joint style for buffer() — the author flagged 'something fancier for nicer joints' but never chose; miter vs round vs bevel will visibly change block corners.
How PerlinNoise was meant to be consumed for water/terrain: domain scaling, octave count and thresholding are all unrecoverable since the class is unused and partly broken.
Whether the modern MFCG still uses this Voronoi core at all — only the CPU-profile and draw-call recordings in captures/ and profiler/ can answer that; this slice cannot.
Does road quality depend on aStar's non-optimality? Replacing it with a correct A* may change road shapes, so it is a behaviour-shift to verify, not a free fix.
Array.sort tie-breaking: MathUtils.sign returns 0 for equidistant seeds, so radial ordering depends on target sort stability — irrelevant for floats, relevant if a rewrite snaps coordinates.

techniques.name: Arced district labels (OBB + double bisection + circular arc)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Min-area OBB gives label orientation; cut polygon by OBB centre-line perpendicular to long axis, take midpoint of that segment as vertical position; cut again parallel to long axis through that point, the segment is the label span and its midpoint the label centre; bend label toward the centroid on a circular arc whose radius R -> infinity when label centre == centroid and R == OBB height at max separation (R = C/|d|). Font height deliberately ignored; no multi-line labels.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Exact radius constant (h^2/|d| vs h^2/2|d|) and which segment is chosen when a cut meets a concave polygon multiple times

techniques.name: Ward mesh: typed cells + typed edges as the city substrate
techniques.algorithm_summary: Warp-mode screenshots show a coarse planar polygon mesh (6-9 sided, ward-sized) drawn in red; mesh edges coincide exactly with streets, cells hold building blocks. Castle occupies exactly one cell (creator-confirmed). City Painter's tool list (paint cells, draw/select edges, build path, collapse edges, merge/cut cells, relax/pinch mesh) plus paints Borough/Farm/Road exposes the same structure; a wall is the boundary edge-cycle of a cell cluster, a road is a selected edge chain.

New one is Voronoi-diagram based, yields irregular 4-7 sided lots tiling the block with a uniform inset gap and interior courtyards. Shipped disabled by default (Style>Buildings>Improved lots) because it crashes occasionally; separate 'No triangles' and 'Tight' flags coexist.

top_insights: Roads inside the walls do not exist as geometry - the creator states they are just the gaps between buildings; only exterior approach roads are drawn polylines. This is the single most load-bearing structural fact in the slice.

The city sits on a coarse typed polygon mesh (ward-sized cells + typed edges). Warp-mode screenshots show mesh edges coinciding exactly with streets, and the creator confirms a castle always occupies exactly one cell. City Painter's tool list (paint cells, collapse edges, merge/cut cells, relax/pinch mesh) is effectively a spec of the data structure.

The arced-label algorithm is fully written out: min-area OBB for orientation, two orthogonal polygon cuts (the second through the midpoint of the first) for position and span, then a circular arc bending toward the centroid with R -> infinity at zero offset and R = OBB height at max separation. Only the radius constant is ambiguous.

Curved streets were prototyped in Sept 2019 and then CUT - 0.8.0's version bump went to Voronoi lots instead, so through 0.8.1 MFCG streets remained straight mesh-edge chains. Anyone assuming MFCG has spline streets in this era is wrong.

0.8.0 replaced recursive block bisection (whose defect was 'a lot of triangles') with a Voronoi-based lot algorithm, shipped disabled by default because it crashed occasionally - a feature-flag failure strategy, not a retry/discard one.
The shoreline was 'always a rough parabola' (peninsula if facing the centre, bay otherwise), and islands plus landlocked lakes are an explicit, deliberate exclusion rather than a missing feature.

Captured live palette hex for all 8 slots (paper D6CCA8, light 947A69, medium 827968, dark 332C24, roof A0846E, water CAC3B3, green 9EA885, road D8CFB0), confirming road defaults to approximately paper.
Population is about 6 persons per building across three observed maps (286/~1800, 856/~5200, 3423/~21000); city size is an integer ward count with min 5 and max 200.
City Painter's sales pitch is the cleanest enumeration of MFCG's hard constraints: circular single-cluster city, one ring wall, radial roads, at most one castle, no islands/ponds/river confluences.

Stated philosophy is simplicity and legibility over correctness - farms are deliberately under-generated because realistic density 'just doesn't look interesting', and generated compass roses were rejected as 'too fancy for pretty minimalistic city maps'.

techniques.name: MINSTD single global PRNG stream
techniques.algorithm_summary: Lehmer LCG seed=(seed*48271.0)%2147483647, multiplier typed Float so the product is exact in double. float()=next()/n; normal()=3 draws averaged; fuzzy(1)=normal(); int(a,z)=1 draw in [a,z-1]. One global static stream drives layout, ward choice and building subdivision in call order. Verified by executing a Python port: seed 682063530 -> first floats 0.380382162, 0.427353017, 0.757494765, 0.029789500.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing; exact and executed. Only risk is a port using 32-bit int maths before the modulo.

techniques.name: Jittered spiral seed placement
techniques.algorithm_summary: 8*nPatches seeds: a = sa + 5*sqrt(i) with sa=U*2pi; r = 0 for i=0 else 10 + i*(2+U). Linear radius growth, angular step ~2.5/sqrt(i) (executed: 5.00, 2.07, 1.59, 1.34, 1.18 rad for i=0..4; 0.25 rad at i=99). i=0 consumes no draw. Gives a tight irregular centre and a regular periphery; index order ~= radius order, which later stages depend on.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Why 5 rad rather than the golden angle 2.39996, and whether the 8x multiplier was tuned or arbitrary.

techniques.name: Bowyer-Watson incremental Voronoi with a padded frame
techniques.algorithm_summary: Frame = bbox padded 25% per side, seeded with two triangles from its 4 corners. addPoint: collect triangles whose circumcircle contains p, find cavity boundary edges via reversed-edge tests, re-fan from p. O(n^2) overall, run 4x per city. Regions = incident triangles sorted CCW by a hand-written half-plane comparator; patch polygon = the triangles' circumcentre Points. partioning() drops any region touching a frame vertex.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Degenerate handling: the circumcentre divides by dx1=p1.y-p2.y and yields NaN on horizontal edges; never fires with continuous input but a port on snapped coords will.

techniques.name: Partial Lloyd relaxation (off-by-four)
techniques.algorithm_summary: 3 passes, each relaxing voronoi.points[0..2] plus points[nPatches]. But points[0..3] are the four FRAME corners (constructor seeds points with them; addPoint only appends), and frame regions never appear in partioning(), so three entries are no-ops. points[nPatches] is input index nPatches-4, and the removal/append shifts it, so the seeds actually relaxed are indices nPatches-4, -3, -2 — one step each, none central, not the citadel. Relax replaces a seed with its region's vertex mean and rebuilds the whole diagram.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether to copy the code (which produces MFCG's look) or the comment's intent (relax the centre + citadel), which produces a different, more uniform centre.

techniques.name: Radial sort and patch role assignment
techniques.algorithm_summary: Sort all points ascending by |p| from the world origin (frame corners sort to the end, ~734 vs 346 half-extent), then enumerate real regions. count==0 -> centre = that patch's vertex nearest the origin, and becomes plaza if plazaNeeded. count==nPatches && citadelNeeded -> citadel (withinCity but never withinWalls). count<nPatches -> withinCity=true, withinWalls=wallsNeeded, pushed to inner.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Why centre is a vertex rather than the patch centroid — it is only used as a street destination and for the buggy distance() cull.

techniques.name: Shared-Point identity as the topology substrate
techniques.algorithm_summary: Patch polygons hold the identical Point objects (Delaunay circumcentres) shared by adjacent cells. All adjacency is reference equality: contains=indexOf, findEdge checks the next vertex is the same object, borders/getNeighbour use reversed edges. Consequence: mutating one Point moves every patch touching it — used deliberately for junction merging, wall smoothing and street smoothing. Requires globally consistent CCW winding.
techniques.biggest_unknown: A port to value types must add an explicit shared vertex table with integer ids; no source says how watabou later handled it (the live build uses a DCEL).

techniques.name: Junction merging at an 8-unit threshold
techniques.algorithm_summary: For each city patch (inner + citadel), scan consecutive vertex pairs; if distinct objects and distance < 8, rebind every other patch's reference from v1 to v0, move v0 to the midpoint (v0+=v1; v0*=0.5), drop v1 from this patch. Then dedupe references in the touched patches. index++ runs unconditionally, so consecutive short edges are not both collapsed, and there is only one pass.
techniques.biggest_unknown: No guard against collapsing a patch below 3 distinct vertices; the damage surfaces later as a bad circumference or failed cut.

techniques.name: findCircumference union outline
techniques.algorithm_summary: An edge (a,b) of any patch in the set is outer iff no patch in the set holds the reversed edge (b,a). Accumulate into parallel arrays A (starts) and B (ends), then walk result.push(A[i]); i = A.indexOf(B[i]) until back to 0. Shortcuts for 0 and 1 patches.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Unhandled: a non-simply-connected union or a pinch vertex appearing twice in A gives a wrong/short loop; a broken chain pushes null (indexOf -> -1) with no guard.

techniques.name: Curtain wall smoothing with reserved vertices
techniques.algorithm_summary: Wall shape = circumference of inner. Every vertex is kept (count never changes); every non-reserved vertex is replaced by smoothVertex(v,f)=(prev+f*v+next)/(2+f) with f=min(1,40/|patches|) — which equals 1 for every reachable size since size is clamped to <=40. Polygon.set writes into the existing Points, so the blocks behind the wall move with it. The single-patch (castle) path aliases the citadel's own polygon array instead.
techniques.biggest_unknown: segments:Array<Bool> is created all-true and never set false; its purpose (watergates?) is unrecorded in 2017.

techniques.name: Gate selection: >=2 inner wards plus cyclic neighbour suppression
techniques.algorithm_summary: Candidates = wall vertices that are not reserved and are shared by more than one walled patch (so a street can leave the vertex inward). Then loop: pick Random.int(0,len), push as a gate, and splice out the pick plus both cyclic neighbours (special-cased at index 0 and len-1); continue while >=3 candidates remain, giving roughly |entrances|/3 gates. Throw 'Bad walled area shape!' on zero candidates or zero gates. Finally each gate vertex is smoothed once more with f=1.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Gate count is purely emergent from wall vertex count; nothing states a target count or spacing in world units.

techniques.name: Outer-ward splitting to create a road stub
techniques.algorithm_summary: If exactly one countryside patch touches a gate, every outward edge is interior to it and no road can leave. Fix: out = rot(-90) of (next(gate)-prev(gate)); farthest = the outer patch vertex maximising (v-gate)·out/|v-gate| excluding wall/reserved vertices; split the patch along gate->farthest into two Patches sharing both endpoints, and replace it in-place in model.patches. Skipped for triangles (length>3 guard).
techniques.biggest_unknown: When the guard rejects a triangle the gate just gets no road (A* returns null and is silently dropped) — no fallback is attempted.

techniques.name: Tower placement
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every non-gate wall vertex with at least one live adjacent segment becomes a tower — no spacing rule, no count target. Radius is a rendering constant, not a model quantity: Brush.THICK_STROKE(1.8) x 1.5 for the castle, x1 for the city wall. buildTowers is gated by the caller (wallsNeeded / castle), not by the always-true `real` field.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether tower radius was ever meant to vary; the live build has CurtainWall.getTowerRadius called 4242 times.

techniques.name: Castle with city-facing gates
techniques.algorithm_summary: Castle builds its own CurtainWall over [citadel] with reserved = every citadel vertex that also touches a non-city patch — i.e. the outward face — so gates are forced onto the town side. Quality gate: citadel compactness (4*pi*A/P^2) < 0.75 throws 'Bad citadel shape!' and rebuilds the whole city. Geometry: shrinkEq(4.0) then createOrthoBuilding(block, sqrt(A)*4, 0.6).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing structural; the live build keeps the same 0.75 threshold but repairs the shape instead of throwing.

techniques.name: Topology: street graph = patch-edge graph with blocked nodes
techniques.algorithm_summary: One node per unique vertex object, one undirected edge per patch edge, cost = Euclidean edge length; no cost shaping at all. blocked = citadel outline + wall outline MINUS gates; a blocked vertex still gets a node and map entries but gets no links, so it is isolated rather than deleted. inner/outer are node exclusion sets: a node joins inner (city patch) or outer (countryside patch) only if it is NOT on the border polygon, which is exactly what leaves gates usable by both searches.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing in-slice; the live build replaced Map<Point,Node> with Topology.getNode (80,876 calls) and excludePoints/excludePolygon.

techniques.name: FIFO pseudo-A* pathfinding
techniques.algorithm_summary: Named aStar but has no heuristic and no priority queue: openSet.shift() pops FIFO, a node closes on first expansion, g-scores are relaxed along the way. Exclusion arrays are seeded straight into the closed set. Paths are therefore NOT guaranteed shortest — the resulting meander is load-bearing aesthetically. buildPath returns the path reversed (goal first), so a street's [0] is the plaza/centre and its last element is the gate.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether the meander was intended or accidental; replacing it with real A* straightens every street and changes the look.

techniques.name: Street and road construction
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per gate: destination = plaza's nearest vertex (plaza acts as a roundabout) else the single centre vertex; A* excluding topology.outer keeps the street inside the city; null throws 'Unable to build a street!' and rebuilds. For city-wall gates only, the road's far end is the topology node nearest gate.norm(1000) — a phantom point 1000 units out along the gate's radial, well beyond the ~346-unit map — then A* excluding topology.inner keeps it outside. A null road is silently dropped. Castle gates get a street but never a road.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing states why street failure is fatal while road failure is not; the live build tolerates both.

techniques.name: Artery stitching and segment dedup
techniques.algorithm_summary: Cut every street and road into consecutive Segments, dropping runs where both endpoints lie on the plaza; dedupe by DIRECTED identity pair (so (a,b) and (b,a) both survive). Then pop segments LIFO and greedily first-fit onto an existing artery's head (unshift) or tail (push), else start a new artery. Single pass, only the two ends are tested, so joinable arteries are never merged — junctions end up as artery endpoints, which is what keeps smoothing from dragging them.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Order depends on pop() order which depends on gate draw order; no source says whether the resulting artery fragmentation was intended.

techniques.name: Street smoothing by shared-Point mutation
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per artery: smoothed = smoothVertexEq(3), i.e. (prev + 3*cur + next)/5 computed with wrap-around; write back only indices 1..len-2 so both endpoints are pinned and the wrap artifacts are discarded. Because the Points are shared, one pass simultaneously curves the street and reshapes every block fronting it — MFCG's curved frontages come free. Order-dependent: later arteries see earlier mutations; a vertex interior to two arteries is smoothed twice. geom/Spline.hx exists but is dead code.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Only one pass and only weight 3 — no source explains the choice; the live build uses Chaikin and Cubic instead.

techniques.name: Ward deck plus rateLocation argmin scoring
techniques.algorithm_summary: Fixed 36-entry deck (Craftsmen 21, Slum 5, Merchant/Patriciate/Market 2 each, Cathedral/Administration/Military/Park 1 each) perturbed by exactly 3 adjacent transpositions (Std.int(36/10)). Position encodes priority: Cathedral at index 5, Administration 14, Market 20, Military 29, Park 32; past 36 patches everything is a Slum. Per class, Reflect looks up a STATIC rateLocation and picks argmin (lower is better, ties go to the earliest/most central patch); classes without one are placed uniformly at random. Order: plaza->Market, then gate wards (p=0.5 walled / 0.2 unwalled per candidate patch), then the deck, then outskirts, then countryside.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Reflect.field on a class does not find inherited statics on Haxe/JS, so CraftsmenWard is placed randomly. A port that DOES inherit gets the constant 0 from Ward.rateLocation, min returns the first patch, and all 21 craftsmen wards lay down in strict centre-outward order — a silent, visible divergence.

techniques.name: Per-ward rateLocation scoring functions
techniques.algorithm_summary: Cathedral: plaza-fronting -> -1/area (biggest wins), else distance*area. Administration: plaza-fronting -> 0, else distance to plaza centre. Merchant: distance to plaza/centre. Slum: negated distance (as far out as possible). Market: +INF if it borders another Market, else area/plaza-area (prefer smallest). Military: 0 if it borders the citadel, 1 if it borders the wall, else +INF unless the city has neither. Patriciate: -1 per already-assigned Park neighbour, +1 per Slum neighbour (so it depends on deck order — parks are placed after the first patriciate).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Five of these call Polygon.distance, which is buggy (returns distance from the polygon's FIRST vertex, never updating its running minimum), biasing every distance-based score by up to a patch radius.

techniques.name: Setback-based street widths (getCityBlock)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Streets are not geometry — they are the gap left by insetting blocks. Per patch edge: 1.0 along the wall, 1.0 on plaza frontage or an artery, 0.5 on ordinary inner edges, 0.3 on outskirt edges (MAIN_STREET 2.0 / REGULAR_STREET 1.0 / ALLEY 0.6, each halved). Convex patches use shrink (successive half-plane cuts); concave ones use buffer (offset each edge, resolve self-intersections by double-inserting each crossing, decompose into loops, keep the largest signed area).
techniques.biggest_unknown: The artery test checks membership not adjacency, so an edge whose endpoints are both on one artery non-consecutively is falsely widened.

techniques.name: Recursive perpendicular-bisection alleys
techniques.algorithm_summary: Split perpendicular to the LONGEST edge (a cheap stand-in for OBB bisection), at ratio (1-0.8*gridChaos)/2 + U*0.8*gridChaos, tilted by up to +/-pi/12*gridChaos — with tilt switched off once area < 4*minSq to keep buildings rectangular. Stop when area < minSq * 2^(4*sizeChaos*(U-0.5)) (a 16x range at sizeChaos 0.8); a finished lot is discarded with probability emptyProb. The recursive `split` flag (alley gap 0.6 vs hairline 0.0) is half.square > minSq/(U*U); the product of two uniforms biases toward 0, so alleys appear mostly at the top of the recursion.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Polygon.cut returns the polygon unchanged when it finds != 2 intersections, so the recursion can spin forever; escape is only the randomised stop threshold. The live build logs 'Failed to make a cut' explicitly.

techniques.name: Axis-locked ortho building subdivision
techniques.algorithm_summary: For monumental buildings (Castle, Cathedral, Farm). Fix two global axes c1 = longest edge vector, c2 = rot90(c1); each recursive cut picks whichever axis is more perpendicular to the current longest edge (smaller |v.c|), at ratio 0.4+U*0.2. Stop below minBlockSq*2^(normal()*2-1); keep a finished cell with probability `fill`. Wrapped in while(true) retry-until-non-empty (safe only because fill is 0.5/0.6/0.8).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Nothing structural; the fill/threshold constants are per-caller and undocumented.

techniques.name: filterOutskirts density thinning
techniques.algorithm_summary: Applied to any CommonWard that is not isEnclosed. Build 'populated edges': arteries weight 1, edges facing a withinCity neighbour weight 1 if that neighbour is enclosed else 0.4, each storing d = the deepest perpendicular distance of any other patch vertex from that line. Per-vertex density: 1 at gates, 2*U if every patch touching it is withinCity, else 0. Per building: minDist = min(perp distance / edge.d), then divide by the inverse-distance interpolation of vertex density at the building centre; keep iff Random.fuzzy(1) > minDist. Result: buildings hug roads and the enclosed side, and the countryside-facing interior thins out.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The 0.4 weight and the 2*U density scale are unexplained tuning constants; the formula's intent is reconstructed, not stated.

techniques.name: Retry-on-exception loop with persistent structural flags
techniques.algorithm_summary: do try { build(); instance=this } catch(e:Error) { trace; instance=null } while (instance==null). Four throw sites: 'Bad walled area shape!' x2 (no gate candidates / zero gates), 'Bad citadel shape!' (compactness<0.75), 'Unable to build a street!' (A* null). Retries CONTINUE the same PRNG stream (Random.reset is outside the loop), and plazaNeeded/citadelNeeded/wallsNeeded are drawn once before it, so a failing seed retries with the same structural intent forever — no cap, no fallback. build() does not reset plaza/citadel to null, so a retry producing fewer regions leaves a dangling citadel reference. catch(e:Error) catches only openfl.errors.Error, so nulls, NaNs and infinite loops escape entirely.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The live build reseeds per attempt instead; which behaviour to adopt is a public-API decision for any shareable-link feature.

techniques.name: Live-MFCG deltas the 2017 design lacks
techniques.algorithm_summary: Console traces name Source/com/watabou/mfcg/model/City.hx:183-191 stages buildPatches, optimizeJunctions, buildDomains, buildWalls, buildStreets, buildCanals, createWards, buildCityTowers, buildGeometry. Call records show Delaunator (O(n log n) triangulation), PoissonPattern.warp/validate (warped blue-noise seeding), DCEL/HalfEdge/Face/EdgeChain/Rib (half-edge mesh), PolyBounds.obb+convexHull paired 215,693 times (real OBB bisection via Bisector), SkeletonBuilder + BuildingPainter.drawRoof (straight-skeleton roofs), PolyBool.and (polygon booleans), Chaikin/Cubic (curve smoothing), Canal/Harbour/addWatergate (water, propose-and-reject: 884 'discard' lines), District/DistrictBuilder/Grower/WardGroup (multi-cell grown districts), Block.indentFronts/TwistedBlock.createLots (lots with frontage), tracery/Markov (names), UnitSystem. Failures are now repaired or logged rather than thrown: Castle 'Bloating the citadel...' then 'Equalizing...' values climbing 0.4675 -> 0.7499 against the SAME 0.75 threshold, and 'Unable to build a street!' appears mid-run without aborting.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Only names, counts and log strings are observable — no algorithm for buildDomains, buildCanals or buildCityTowers is recoverable from this slice's evidence.

top_insights: The whole 2017 design rests on one decision: adjacent patches hold the IDENTICAL Point objects (Delaunay circumcentres), so all adjacency is reference equality and mutating a vertex moves every patch touching it. Junction merging, wall smoothing and street smoothing are all the same trick — smoothing a street bends the blocks either side for free. A port to value types must add a shared vertex table with integer ids or reproduce nothing.

Three sizeable bugs are load-bearing for MFCG's look and a re-implementer must decide about each: Polygon.distance never updates its running minimum (returns distance from the polygon's FIRST vertex — used by the patch cull and five ward scores); the relaxation's toRelax indices are off by four because points[0..3] are the Voronoi frame corners, so it relaxes three no-ops plus index nPatches-4 instead of the centre and citadel; and Graph.aStar has no heuristic and no priority queue (FIFO, closed on first pop), so streets are not shortest paths and meander characteristically.

Streets are not drawn geometry inside the city — they are the negative space left by inset blocks. getCityBlock sets back 1.0 along the wall and main streets, 0.5 along ordinary inner edges and 0.3 along outskirt edges (MAIN_STREET 2.0 / REGULAR_STREET 1.0 / ALLEY 0.6, halved). Only outward roads get an actual two-pass casing stroke.

Ward placement is a fixed 36-card deck (21 Craftsmen, 5 Slum, ...) consumed in order with only three adjacent transpositions of shuffling, so deck POSITION is the priority schedule: Cathedral is placed 6th while good plaza-adjacent patches are free, Park 33rd, and everything past 36 patches is a Slum. Selection is argmin of a static rateLocation, with classes lacking one placed uniformly at random.

Determinism is fragile in two specific ways a port will get wrong: Haxe's lazy ternaries and short-circuits mean the spiral's i==0 consumes NO draw and Random.fuzzy(0) consumes none, and Reflect.field does not find inherited statics on Haxe/JS — if a port's inheritance DOES find Ward.rateLocation (constant 0), all 21 craftsmen wards lay down in strict centre-outward order instead of randomly.

The retry loop continues the same PRNG stream and re-draws nothing structural: plazaNeeded/citadelNeeded/wallsNeeded are fixed before the loop, so a chronically bad seed retries the same intent with no cap and no fallback. The live MFCG reseeds per attempt instead — visible in the console as '>> seed:777001' then two different '-->>' seeds.

The live trace shows every 2017 stage internal was replaced while the stage skeleton survived: Delaunator for Bowyer-Watson, warped Poisson-disc for the spiral, a DCEL for shared-Point arrays, real OBB bisection (PolyBounds.obb + convexHull paired 215,693 times) for perpendicular-to-longest-edge cuts, straight-skeleton roofs, polygon booleans, and three new stages (buildDomains, buildCanals, buildCityTowers). The 0.75 citadel compactness threshold survives verbatim but is now repaired by iterative 'Bloating/Equalizing' (observed 0.4675 climbing to 0.7499) instead of throwing.
open_questions: Copy the relaxation off-by-four (which yields MFCG's look) or the comment's stated intent (relax the centre and citadel, giving a more uniform centre)? No source says which watabou believed he shipped.
Reproduce Polygon.distance's first-vertex bug? Five ward scores and the radius*3 patch cull depend on it; fixing it changes every map and is a legitimate behaviour shift that must be recorded.
Keep the FIFO pseudo-A*? True A* straightens streets; the meander appears to be part of the aesthetic but may be accidental.
What is the 8x seed multiplier actually for — countryside extent, boundary quality, or arbitrary? It dominates runtime via the O(n^2) triangulation of 8*nPatches points.
Why is the spiral angle constant 5 rad rather than the golden angle 2.39996? The resulting large irregular centre and regular periphery may be accidental.
What was CurtainWall.segments:Array<Bool> for? Never set false in 2017; the live addWatergate/splitSegment strongly suggest water gaps, but the 2017 intent is unrecorded.
How should gate count scale with city size? It is purely emergent (|entrances|/3); a different wall shape silently changes it.
Should the retry loop reseed (live MFCG) or continue the stream (2017)? The two give different distributions for 'what seed N looks like' — an API-shaped decision for shareable links.

What cost model do streets deserve? Edge cost here is pure Euclidean length; MFCG's visible preference for reusing corridors is an accident of BFS order plus tidyUpRoads deduplication, not a modelled bias.
What is the world unit? Nothing states a scale (MAIN_STREET 2.0, seed spacing ~2.5); the live build has a UnitSystem class, so a real scale was added later.

Does the algorithm need an explicit failure taxonomy? 2017 throws on 4 conditions and silently swallows at least 5 more (null road, unsplit triangle, failed cut, degenerate patch, broken circumference chain); the live build logs every one of these by name.
