top_insights: UNIT CORRECTION for the whole project: the task brief's '3500 m settlement width' is wrong for this capture. blankSettlementWidth=3500 applies only to size BLANK; presets.json gives CITY width=5000 m, so 500000 units = 5000 m and 1 coordinate unit = 1 CENTIMETRE. Confirmed independently by roadLength params reproducing as measured edge modes and by the on-screen scale bar.

The 15-degree max-turn clamp is FTG's single most identifiable geometric fingerprint and is directly measurable: 1-degree histograms of degree-2 turn deviation are populated at 10-14 deg and exactly EMPTY at 15+ for edge types 0/1/2/10. An original generator should use a different mechanism (splines, tensor fields) rather than a per-vertex angle clamp.

create-request.json is the highest-value artefact in the capture: FTG's entire tuning surface is client-visible because the client POSTs it - staged spoke growth params, 17 district archetypes with weighted plot-decoration tables, 209 building types with a resource dependency graph, climate/tree proportions, the lot and wall placement modes. These are the creator's own names, so they are STATED, not inferred.

FTG's 'building' is a ~20x20 m, ~433 m2 compound with ~5 sub-locations (rooms) - not a medieval cottage. 2798 buildings for a 9500 target population = 3.4 people per building. Any original generator copying FTG's look must decide whether to adopt that entity granularity, because it drives the room/person model.

Street geometry is locally orthogonal but globally unaligned: junction arm angles median 90.02 deg with 56% in the 80-100 band, yet the global heading spectrum is flat (max 10-deg bin only 8.0%). Each branch lattice carries its own arbitrary rotation. That combination is what produces the 'organic but rectilinear' read.

Two cheap choices are visible in the statistics and are easy to beat: trees are NOT Poisson-disc (nearest-neighbour min 0.28 m, no hard floor), and sprite variants are assigned round-robin (590/590/589x5 over 4125 trees), with every serialised scale exactly 1.0.

The shipped payload contains real defects: one of four district rings self-intersects (rasterised area 4.47x the shoelace area), every ring has duplicate consecutive vertices, the shortest road edge is 0.01 m, one building centroid sits at y = -39 m outside the declared extent, and 3.9% of buildings have no entrance point. Consumers must fill rings even-odd and sanitise.

Generation is entirely server-side and SLOW: ~300 s wall per CITY create with the client idle (busy 4.6 s), and the client shows only a spinner. That is a product constraint an original generator competing on interactivity can attack directly.

Blocks are the faces of the road graph: block edge lengths cluster at 30 m (43%) and 60 m, exactly the stage roadLength parameters. Median block 1764 m2 holding 3.39 buildings at ~57% coverage, 12.9% of blocks left empty.

The Foundry module reveals the event contract without any bundle reading: a stateId optimistic-concurrency token accompanies every mutation and is fanned out over Foundry's socket so all clients resync, and the module overlays an iframe on a fixed 5000x5000 scene - which is exactly the CITY map width in metres, i.e. 1 Foundry unit = 1 m.

techniques.name: City.build nine-stage pipeline with whole-city retry loop
techniques.algorithm_summary: buildPatches, optimizeJunctions, buildDomains, buildWalls, buildStreets(+tidyUpRoads), buildCanals run inside a retry loop that re-rolls the seed on failure; createWards, buildCityTowers, buildGeometry then run once. Proven by the build's own Stopwatch traces (City.hx:183-191) plus call counts: loop-body functions run N times for N attempts, post-loop functions exactly once.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What buildCityTowers does (always 0 ms, no dedicated class executed).

techniques.name: Patch seeding: exactly 8*size+4 points, Delaunator + DCEL
techniques.algorithm_summary: Delaunator.circumradius2 == 8*size+4 in all 7 builds (204/212/316/644). mapbox-delaunator port (pseudoAngle, hashKey, legalize, orientIfSure), getVoronoi once, then a half-edge DCEL; Face.new==Cell.new==n-|hull|. Ancestor used nPatches*8 on a jittered Vogel spiral.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Exact spiral constants in 0.11.x and where the +4 points sit.

techniques.name: Coastline from 6-octave fractal Perlin, sampled per cell
techniques.algorithm_summary: Perlin.get / Noise.get == 6.000 exactly in every coast=1 sample; Noise.get count ~= cell count; both are zero whenever coast=0. The `sea` URL param is the sea direction in units of pi radians CCW from screen-East (5/5 screenshots agree).
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the directional gradient and the noise are combined into the land/water test, and the threshold.

techniques.name: buildDomains: DCEL split + floodFill along the water boundary
techniques.algorithm_summary: DCEL.split and DCEL.floodFill run exactly 2x per attempt when coast=1 and 0x when coast=0; City.splitEdge likewise. Inferred: cut the cell mesh along the coastline and flood-fill connected land components.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What a 'domain' is consumed by downstream.

techniques.name: OBB-driven recursive lot subdivision (Bisector)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Bisector.{partition,subdivide,split,makeCut,isSmallEnough,detectStraight}; subdivide calls PolyBounds.obb (convexHull + PolyTransform.asRotateYX, all 1:1) on ~80% of nodes; makeCut==PointExtender.project 1:1. Two levels: ward->blocks (with alley gap) and block->lots (~18.6 lots/block). Replaces the ancestor's area+longest-edge Cutter.bisect recursion; detectStraight snaps cuts to collinear runs.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The stop threshold on OBB dimensions and the chaos parameters (2017's minSq/gridChaos/sizeChaos/emptyProb).

techniques.name: Block.filterInner + Block.indentFronts (polygon boolean setback)
techniques.algorithm_summary: filterInner runs once per createLots (drops lots with no street frontage -> empty courtyards); indentFronts runs once per Block and calls PolyBool.and -> augmentPolygons ~8.8x, i.e. intersect the block with an inset copy to set building fronts back from the street. augmentPolygons is the hottest model function (31.8 ms self).
techniques.biggest_unknown: The inset distance and whether the setback is per-edge or uniform.

techniques.name: Density falloff via ear-clip + barycentric interpolation
techniques.algorithm_summary: Triangulation.earcut == WardGroup.filter 1:1; WardGroup.getTris == interpolate 1:1; GeomUtils.barycentric / interpolate = 8.47. Ward polygon is ear-clipped once (~9 tris), then each candidate building's centre is located and its survival probability barycentrically interpolated from per-vertex density. Direct descendant of 2017 Ward.filterOutskirts.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the per-vertex density values are assigned in 0.11.x.

techniques.name: Canal: two river modes, generate-and-test with a ~40-try budget
techniques.algorithm_summary: regularRiver when coast=0, deltaRiver when coast=1 (4/4 exact, distinguished by two different 'discard' trace sites Canal.hx:216 vs :268). Courses come from Topology.buildPath -> Graph.aStar, each rejection logs 'discard'; successes used 1/8/11 discards, failures 35-41 then City.hx:156 throws and the whole city restarts. 7 of 10 attempts failed at size=80 with river+coast. City.getCanalWidth gives a variable-width ribbon.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What validateCourse actually tests (length? sinuosity? crossings?) and the exact try budget.

techniques.name: Citadel repair loop (Castle.equalize) replacing 2017's reject
techniques.algorithm_summary: Trace 'Equalizing... <compactness>' fires once per Castle.equalize call; all 57 traced values are strictly below 0.75, monotonically rising, 1-20 iterations. Only consistent loop: while(compactness<0.75){trace(c); equalize();}. 0.75 is the ancestor's 'Bad citadel shape!' threshold; the live build repairs instead of throwing. 'Bloating the citadel...' is a separate prior repair.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What equalize() actually moves (edge-length equalisation is the best fit) and what 'bloating' does.

techniques.name: Straight skeleton -> district ridge -> curved label
techniques.algorithm_summary: SkeletonBuilder.run tracks District.new; output feeds District.getRidge -> annotations.Ridge.build -> Equator.build/largestSpan -> PolyUtils.simplify==visvalingam (1:1) -> Cubic.smoothOpen -> CurvedLabel with one _CurvedLabel.Letter per character positioned by PathTracker.getPos/get_tangent.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Which skeleton path is chosen as the ridge and how the label size is fitted to it.

techniques.name: PoissonPattern: static Bridson blue-noise, k=50, 140 points
techniques.algorithm_summary: Built once in a static initialiser before Main.new (6-11 ms); warp/step == validate/step == 50.000 exactly; 230 steps, 140 emitted. Never called during a city build in any recording.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Which subsystem consumes the pattern - no call site was observed.

techniques.name: Casing+core two-pass stroking for all linear features
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every road/street/river polyline is stroked twice: colorDark at (core + 2t) then colorRoad/colorWater at core, where t is the single per-map outline width from Style.getStrokeWidth. The identity casing - core == 2t holds exactly in all 7 draw records (t = 0.119/0.121/0.143/0.245/0.556/0.578/0.905). Wall 1.9, grid 0.267, scale/compass 0.533, road core 2.0 are scale-invariant constants.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How t is derived from the map scale.

techniques.name: Building = dark footprint + offset colorRoof polygon
techniques.algorithm_summary: BuildingPainter.g -> GraphicsExtender.drawPolygon filled #1a1917 (colorDark); BuildingPainter.drawRoof -> GraphicsExtender.drawPolygonAt filled #a5a095 (colorRoof), counts identical 1:1 in all 7 samples. Then 3 strokes at width t. 96% of fills have 5-8 segments. drawSolids handles the black landmark buildings.
techniques.biggest_unknown: The roof offset vector (constant? per-ward? derived from a light direction?).

techniques.name: Palette as data: six JSON colour schemes with tint and weathering
techniques.algorithm_summary: Assets/{default,ink,bw,vivid,modern,natural}.json, 13 keys each: colorPaper/Light/Dark/Roof/Water/Wall/Green/Tree/Label/Road, tintStrength, tintMethod in {Brightness,Spectrum,Overlay}, weathering. Style.getTint and Style.spectrum are each called exactly once per District (7/7 samples) -> one tint per district. techniques.name: Tiered failure policy (repair / local retry / skip / full restart)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Repair for shape quality (citadel equalize, bloat); local retry for path search (canal discard); silent skip for local geometry ('Unable to build a street!', 'Failed to create a non-empty alleys group', '(0) Failed to make a cut' - all downgraded from the ancestor's throws); full restart with a new seed only for a missing canal. At size 80 that last tier restarted 7 of 10 attempts.

top_insights: Patch seeding is still the 2017 formula: Delaunator.circumradius2 == 8*size+4 to the unit in all 7 recorded builds (204/212/316/644) - the clearest surviving link to TownGeneratorOS, whose Model.buildPatches wrote `for (i in 0...nPatches * 8)`.

The retry boundary is provable from call counts: buildPatches..buildCanals run once per attempt (7x in one size-80 sample), while createWards/buildCityTowers/buildGeometry/Bisector/District/Namer run exactly once. Canal failure is the only condition that restarts a whole city - and it fired on 7 of 10 attempts at size=80 with river+coast.

Lot subdivision moved from area-driven to OBB-driven: Bisector.subdivide calls PolyBounds.obb (== convexHull == PolyTransform.asRotateYX, all 1:1) on ~80% of recursion nodes. This, plus the new detectStraight and a real polygon-boolean setback (Block.indentFronts -> PolyBool.and), is why 0.11.x lots are rectangular where 2017's were slivers.

Every linear feature is a two-pass casing+core stroke: casing = core + 2t, verified exactly in all seven draw records across seven different t values (0.119 to 0.905). Buildings are a colorDark footprint plus a colorRoof polygon drawn at an offset (drawPolygonAt count == drawRoof count, 1:1, 7/7).

Three shipped assets give exact ground truth that no amount of profiling could: grammar.json (4401 B, the full district/city naming grammar with feature guards CASTLE?/WALLS?/COAST?/RIVER?/PLAZA?/TEMPLE?/UNIQUE?/COMPACT?), six palette JSONs (colorPaper #CCC5B8 and colorDark #1A1917 unchanged since 2017; ink.json is Palette.INK verbatim), and four Markov corpora (english/given_male/given_female/elven).

The citadel is repaired, not rejected: all 57 traced 'Equalizing... <compactness>' values are strictly below the ancestor's 0.75 threshold and rise monotonically, which pins the loop shape to `while (c < 0.75) { trace(c); equalize(); }`.
`sea` is a direction, not a level: sea*pi radians CCW from screen-East, confirmed against five screenshots (0=E, 0.3=NE, 0.6=NNW, 1=W, 1.8=SE).

Cost is overwhelmingly buildGeometry (80-93% of model time: 11 ms at size 24, 260 ms at size 80) and the OpenFL Canvas2D replay (170-230 ms for one size-80 frame, 345k lineTo / 104k stroke calls). A* still uses the 2017 O(V) open-set scan - ObjectMap.keys alone is 15.8 ms of a 44 ms pathfind.

PoissonPattern is a static, page-lifetime blue-noise constant: Bridson with k=50 (warp/step == validate/step == 50.000), 140 points from 230 steps, built before Main.new and never touched during a build in any recording.

The ward taxonomy collapsed: 2017's 13 ward classes and 36-entry WARDS deck became Alleys + a handful of specials (Market, Cathedral, Castle, Harbour, Park, Farm, Wilderness), with all flavour moved up into grown District regions (DistrictBuilder + Grower/DocksGrower/ParkGrower) whose names come from the eight per-type Tracery rule sets.

techniques.name: Water body as deflected level-set + chain extraction
techniques.algorithm_summary: Region.createWater -> Water.river()/pond() -> setLevel() -> createDeflection() (50-73ms self, no children) then buildCurves()->linkSegments(). Result is a polygon kept as open bank chains (87/117/111 segs for a confluence = 3 chains; 2 for river, 1 for coast), smoothed by Chaikin.
techniques.biggest_unknown: createDeflection's inner loop: grid-based level field vs radial deflection of a base primitive

techniques.name: Shoreline depth bands (shallowBands)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Fill water polygon in waterDeep, then stroke the boundary chains k=shallowBands..1 with lineWidth = W*k^1.5 and colour lerp(waterDeep,waterShallow,k/bands), clipped by the water polygon used as an OpenFL mask. Width ratios 5.196:2.828:1 = 3^1.5:2^1.5:1 identical across 3 runs. Plus bands-1 waterTide 1px lines (2N-3 segs = two offset copies per chain).
techniques.biggest_unknown: why the three band strokes have differing segment counts (147/219/439) for one boundary

techniques.name: Elevation: 128x128 fractal Perlin + river carving
techniques.algorithm_summary: Noise.getMap samples a 128x128 grid (16384 = setPixel32 count = dist2poly count); ~5.2 Perlin octaves per sample. createGradient always; createMount/createRidge/createCrack tag-gated. digRiver subtracts f(dist2poly) — O(cells x water segments), measured exactly 41.0 and 36.0 segments per cell.
techniques.biggest_unknown: the exact height falloff used by digRiver and the mount/ridge/crack primitives

techniques.name: Lambert hillshade from grid normals + stack blur
techniques.algorithm_summary: Shading.update computes Vector3D.crossProduct/normalize exactly 16129 = 127^2 times (one normal per interior cell of the 128^2 grid), writes 16384 pixels into a 128x128 BitmapData, applies BlurFilter (lime StackBlur), composites over the map.
techniques.biggest_unknown: light vector, response curve, and the composite/blend mode over the ground colour

techniques.name: Relief as contour-walking hachure (LevelsView + NewGrass)
techniques.algorithm_summary: LevelsView.init once per iso-level polyline (79-114/map), then makeStep walks it (~7k-11k steps); NewGrass.verifySlope gates each step (97-98% pass) and NewGrass.draw emits a 4-point, 0.5px round-capped tuft in ground[1] or ground[2] chosen by slope/aspect. Palette key relief switches Grass/Hachures/Contours.
techniques.biggest_unknown: level spacing rule, step length, and the exact slope test that picks dark vs light

techniques.name: Agent-based road growth (Trackers)
techniques.algorithm_summary: 4-11 Trackers each advance ~30-40 steps; per step flexibility() -> Network.findRoadAhead() -> avoidWater() -> endBridge() -> advance() (counts equal within 1%). getTrackersAround ~5x/step for separation; validateJunctions ~0.6/step; branch/branchFrom spawn side roads; startBridge only where water is crossed.
techniques.biggest_unknown: flexibility() turn-budget curve and the merge/junction acceptance criteria

techniques.name: Highway: edge-to-edge road with global validation + seed retry
techniques.algorithm_summary: Region.initHighway + randomEdge pick a start on a random map border. VillageScene.hx:275 rejects the whole village on 'The highway intersects itself', 'The highway is terminated by water', 'Unfinished bridge on the highway'; the map is re-rolled from a new seed and the failed seed is carried into the URL as &trees=<failed seed>.

techniques.name: Buildings by rejection sampling along frontages
techniques.algorithm_summary: Region.buildAlong per street; each candidate Building.new -> validateBuilding -> testVsRoad + getBuildingsAround (33-43 neighbour queries each, via a BinGrid spatial hash). Acceptance 63-82%; occasional removeBuilding. addBuilding count minus removeBuilding equals the console's building count exactly.

techniques.name: Farmland: Voronoi ∩ land + recursive OBB bisection
techniques.algorithm_summary: getVoronoi -> intersect (PolyBool.and) -> per region cut -> Bisector.partition -> recursive subdivide while area > getMinArea, cutting across the OBB long axis (PolyBounds.obb built on convexHull; counts identical). Then pickLots/filterLots choose ploughed fields, semiSmooth + getArc/getCircle round corners, fixTrails reconciles paths.

techniques.name: Forest: domain-warped Poisson-disc -> Voronoi -> DCEL flood-fill patches
techniques.algorithm_summary: PoissonPattern with exactly k=50 candidates per step (validate/step = 50.00 in all 4 runs), every candidate passed through warp() first; Delaunator builds the Voronoi; DCEL.floodFill labels cells by a Noise threshold, outline + shrink/shrinkExcl give patch polygons; ~50% of candidate trees survive.

techniques.name: Palisade: convex hull -> 32-segment cubic spline -> raster collision -> gates
techniques.algorithm_summary: getPopulated/getBuildings -> ConvexHull.ofSet over 91 points -> poly2smooth -> cubic x32 closed spline; overlaps() == BitMap.check() == 1463 occupancy tests (blocks 337) push the wall off buildings; addGate x3 where roads cross, validateGate x5, getClosestSeg x20. Rendered as a bead of round posts with per-gate passage shadows.

techniques.name: Palette-driven style with closed outline/detail colour formulas
techniques.algorithm_summary: outlineColour = blend(fill, ink, outlineFactor x pressure), detailColour = blend(fill, ink, detailFactor x pressure); outlineFactor defaults 1.0, overridden by outlineRoads/outlineFields. Verified to +/-0.005 on 8 measured colours. Implemented via Color.hardLight (call count identical to Style.getOutline).

techniques.name: Layer order and per-primitive geometry
techniques.algorithm_summary: Bottom-to-top: shading bitmap, relief hachure, roads (green casing w=core+2 then road core; smallRoad 2, largeRoad 6; 6-seg apron per building; square as a 44-gon), fields (fill+outline+dashed furrows), sand banks (w16 @50% + w8), water mask, water+bands, shore outline+tide+bridges, shadows, buildings, trees (one layer per patch), DramaticLight (2 gradients on 1101x1101), 2 fillText labels.

techniques.name: Tree rendering: prototype cloud crowns + linear gradient + flat offset shadow
techniques.algorithm_summary: Crown segment counts are always 4k+1 (153-189) => a 38-47 vertex base polygon smoothed by two Chaikin passes. getCloudCrown runs 0-51 times for 546-751 trees, so crowns are cached prototypes scaled/translated per instance. Each tree: linear-gradient fill, w1 outline, w0.5 interior detail (~85% of crown segs). Shadow = same polygon filled flat in shadowColor, offset by shadowAngle/shadowLength.

techniques.name: Gable-roof building rendering
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per building: 3 quad faces (shadedFace = 3x building count) each fill + w0.5 same-colour stroke; 3 hatch lines crossing the ridge so the hatch colour alternates between lit and shaded plane; 8-segment footprint outline at w1; 3-segment entrance mark. roofSlope sets the ridge; roofLight is a weighted list (default gives ~1/3 slate-blue roofs).

techniques.name: Naming: tag-conditioned Tracery + Markov syllables + shrinking
techniques.algorithm_summary: 69-symbol grammar.json with two extensions: TAG?-rule (eligible only if the model carries that tag: 21 tags incl. WATER/SHORE/RIVER/HILL/VALLEY/FORK/MOUTH/PALISADE/JUCTION[sic]) and p?-rule (probability weight), plus {a|b} alternation and optional letters. DeckRuleSelector draws without replacement. Markov built from given-name lists supplies invented syllables; VillageGrammar.shrink + Syllables.pinch shortens over-long names (logged verbatim).

techniques.algorithm_summary: Params.randomTags then Params.resolve produce the request tags (11 observed in URLs: river/pond/coast/confluence/grove/isolated/dead end/highway/palisade/no square/sparse); Region.updateTags writes back descriptive tags consumed by the grammar. Blueprint.is(tag) is queried 63-92 times per generation, so tags steer the model throughout.

top_insights: The whole look is data-driven by a ~40-key palette JSON (6 themes shipped); three keys are algorithm switches, not colours: relief {Grass|Hachures|Contours}, roofType {Gable|Hip|Flat}, treeShape {Cotton|Conifer|Palm}.
Outline and hatch colours follow a closed formula: blend(fill, ink, factor x pressure), verified to +/-0.005 on 8 independently measured colours.

Water depth shading = base fill + shallowBands nested shoreline strokes clipped by a mask, widths exactly W*k^1.5 (5.196:2.828:1), colours lerp(waterDeep,waterShallow,k/bands) — identical ratios in 3 runs.
Poisson-disc sampling uses exactly k=50 candidates per step, all evaluated, in a warped domain: validate/step = 50.00 in all four coverage runs.
Heightmap is 128x128 and shading normals are the 127x127 interior (16384 and 16129 call counts) — a Lambert hillshade, stack-blurred and composited.
Roads are grown by agent Trackers with a fixed per-step protocol (flexibility -> findRoadAhead -> avoidWater -> endBridge -> advance), ~200 steps from 4-11 agents.
Generation validates and retries: three verbatim highway failures at VillageScene.hx:275, and the rejected seed survives in the URL as &trees=<failed seed>, i.e. vegetation has its own RNG stream.
Relief is a contour engine — LevelsView walks 79-114 iso-lines and emits a 4-point 0.5px tuft per step; on a sparse map the topographic ring structure is plainly visible.
Water generation dominates cost (50-87ms of a 40-160ms model); with no water the whole model is 13.6ms. River carving is naive O(cells x boundary segments) = 41 segment tests per grid cell.
Farmland uses the same OBB-bisection primitive MFCG uses for wards (PolyBounds.obb on convexHull), with identical call counts proving Farmland.cut == Bisector.partition and getMinArea == subdivide.
~85% of all JS calls are OpenFL retained-mode plumbing; the actual algorithm is only a few hundred thousand calls, so a batched-path re-implementation would be far cheaper.

VG and MFCG share the entire com.watabou.geom / geom.polygons / utils / tracery / nlp / coogee substrate — Delaunator, DCEL, PolyBool/Bounds/Core/Cut/Transform/Create, Chaikin, ConvexHull, Perlin/Noise, Palette, BinGrid.

techniques.name: makeCut: convex hull -> OBB -> cut perpendicular to long axis
techniques.algorithm_summary: PolyBounds.obb == PolyBounds.convexHull exactly (hull + rotating calipers). obb:makeCut ratio 2.31/2.27/2.04/2.35 => ~2 OBBs per cut. MathUtils.gate ~1.8x makeCut clamps the split parameter; ArrayExtender.revert ~1.15x reverses winding after split. makeCut is 2938 B, the largest generation routine.

techniques.algorithm_summary: detectStraight = makeCut - Street.new EXACTLY in all four runs (1334-65=1269, 1299-63=1236, 1334-42=1292, 1021-61=960). So the flag is ON for lot subdivision and OFF for the hood-level street subdivision. Produces the terraced-row look: party walls perpendicular to the street, streets at free angles.

Hood.semiSmooth (795B) and getStreetWidth (197B) are 1:1 with streets. semiSmooth is NOT Chaikin (Chaikin counts match greens, not streets). Rendered widths 4.55-11.45 px, one per street, cap=square.

techniques.algorithm_summary: Hood.getCloud 1-2x; Hood.getCircle = Hood.getArc = geom.Circle.new = 17/30/19/30 (lockstep). Screenshots show lumpy lobed silhouettes; one map has a straight chord (a slice of a larger city). createShape is 1434 B.

techniques.name: Road corridor stripe + block setback (indentFronts)
techniques.algorithm_summary: PolyCreate.stripe (748B) called exactly once per street, in the MODEL, never by the renderer (which strokes a polyline). Normal.indentFronts (384B) is 1:1 with Normal blocks and drives PolyBool.and (874/801/650/680 ~ 1.1x buildings). Read as: stripe makes the carriageway polygon, indentFronts does lot AND inset(block).

techniques.name: Lot validation and discard (perimeter-block development)
techniques.algorithm_summary: validateOuter (2225/2145/2066/1720) ~2.9x validateLot (955/908/792/744). Lot leaves ~1333 vs buildings 779 => only 58% of lots get a building; lots that lose street frontage after setback are DISCARDED, not retried. techniques.name: Building = oriented rectangle + ridge, mostly single-wing
techniques.algorithm_summary: Rect.ofPoly (39B, delegates to PolyBounds.obb) ~ buildings. Rect.getRidge ~ wings. Rect.swapAxes fires on ~36% of wings (gable vs eaves to street). Wing.new = Building.new + 8..21, so nearly every building is one rectangle; buildSimple/buildT/buildCross/buildLarge/addBeam fire only 0-8 times per map (landmarks).

techniques.name: Roof colour variation = pure RGB multiply by a pseudo-normal scalar
techniques.algorithm_summary: Over 1742 lit-roof fills: hue sd 0.0012, saturation sd 0.0026 (quantisation only), R/G/B ratios identical to 4 d.p. => a scalar multiply. k: mean 1.000, sd 0.069, range 0.79-1.22, bell-shaped. varRoof=0.3; 0.3 x 0.2357 = 0.0707, and 0.2357 = sd of (sum of 6 uniforms - 3)/3. Counts: Palette.weighted == Color.scale, once per wing.
techniques.biggest_unknown: whether the pseudo-normal is exactly 6 uniforms or another n

techniques.name: getDark: shaded roof face = lit x lerp(colorAmbience, colorShadow, shadowAlpha)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Measured dark/light = (0.7873, 0.8015, 0.8336), sd 0.011-0.012. lerp(#FFFFFF, #7A8499, 0.41)/255 = (0.7863, 0.8024, 0.8361) - matches to 0.5%. shadowAlpha = 0.4 in default.json. getDark is 74 B (one expression); Color.multiply ~ once per wing. Trees use the same formula with t ~ 0.17 instead of 0.41.
techniques.biggest_unknown: the residual 0.5-0.9% discrepancy vs t=0.40 exactly

techniques.name: hatchRoof: chord by PolyCut.pierce, drawn as two tapered filled triangles
techniques.algorithm_summary: EVERY #222222 fill in the buildings layer has exactly 3 segments (5150/11330/5959/8446, zero exceptions) = a triangle. shortStroke/pierce = 2.0004/2.015/2.012/2.011 => exactly 2 tapered triangles per chord, meeting at the midpoint. PolyCut.cut == hatchRoof exactly (splits the roof at the ridge). 17.4 hatch marks per wing, histogram dominated by EVEN counts. Never-run siblings longStroke (624B) and attackDecay0 (65B) confirm the stroke-envelope vocabulary.

techniques.name: Prism shadow: translate footprint once, emit one quad per silhouette edge
techniques.algorithm_summary: drawPrismShadow ~ Wing.new (1:1); PolyTransform.translate ~ wings (1:1); but quad fills per wing = 2.33/2.33/2.43/2.31. Roof faces are 4-gons 55-62%, 5-gons 30-33%, 6-gons 5-9% => expected silhouette edges ~n/2 ~ 2.3. Whole layer is one flat colour under a layer alpha = shadowAlpha; each quad fill is followed by a same-colour w1 stroke of the identical path (half-pixel dilation to kill seams). No hull, no boolean union - the opaque building overdraws the overlap.

techniques.algorithm_summary: The shadow layer's blob-fill segment histogram is BIT-IDENTICAL to the tree-crown fill histogram ({121:5,125:2,129:9,133:6,135:1,137:27,141:14,145:68,...,181:6}), and counts match exactly: 314 trees, 314 tree shadows across the four draw runs. techniques.name: One global blue-noise Poisson field per map, clipped per polygon
techniques.algorithm_summary: PoissonPattern.new is called EXACTLY ONCE per generation while fill is called 29/31/11/36x. warp == validate exactly at 6400/6100/6450/6250 - nearly constant and independent of green count (6400 = 80^2). step 128/122/129/125, emit 80/81/82/78; warp/emit ~ 80, step/emit ~ 1.6. techniques.algorithm_summary: Rigid 6-op signature per tree in 314/314 cases: fill(crown-dark, 121-181 segs) + stroke w1 outline + terminator + fill(light cap, 47-69 segs, ~0.38x) + terminator + stroke w0.6 detail (77-327 segs). techniques.name: Cost model: hatching dominates the view, bisection dominates the model, rasterisation dominates both
techniques.algorithm_summary: Regeneration MapScene.reset = 38.8/47.1/10.4 ms. Model (gen-2, 21.2 ms): Bisector.partition 7.2 (42% of populate), PolyBool.and 3.8, validateOuter 1.6. View (25.9 ms): hatchRoof 9.3 (36%), Roads 4.3, trees 3.1, shadows 1.8. Rasterisation Context3DShape.render 73.3 ms - MORE than the whole generation. Hottest generator routine is GeomUtils.intersectLines (140k-213k calls, 7.8 ms self). openfl.geom.Point.new is called 385k-561k times per generation - allocation pressure is the main re-implementation hazard. Cold start wastes 204.7 ms on lime.media.AudioContext.new in a silent app.

top_insights: Blocks = streets + 1, EXACTLY, in all four runs (66/65, 64/63, 43/42, 62/61). The street network is not grown or graph-built: it IS a single recursive binary bisection of the hood polygon, where every cut simultaneously creates one street and one new block. This is the structural keystone of the whole generator.

detectStraight = makeCut - Street.new, exactly, in all four runs. The same Bisector runs twice with one flag flipped: OFF for the hood-level street cuts (streets may run at any angle), ON for lot cuts (lot boundaries snap perpendicular to the street frontage). One boolean produces the entire terraced-row aesthetic.

Roof hatching is drawn as filled 3-segment TRIANGLES, never as strokes: every one of the 5150/11330/5959/8446 #222222 fills in the buildings layer has exactly 3 segments, and GraphUtils.shortStroke / PolyCut.pierce = 2.00 exactly, i.e. each roof chord becomes two tapered slivers meeting at its midpoint. ~17.4 per wing, ~36% of all view time.

Roof shading is measurable to three decimals and has a physical formula: dark/light = (0.7873, 0.8015, 0.8336), which is lit x lerp(colorAmbience #FFFFFF, colorShadow #7A8499, ~0.41) to within 0.5%, and shadowAlpha is 0.4. Roof colour variation is a pure RGB multiply (hue sd 0.0012, sat sd 0.0026) by k = 1 + varRoof*N with N a 6-uniform pseudo-normal (predicted sd 0.0707, measured 0.069).

Shadows never compute a silhouette hull: drawPrismShadow translates the footprint once and emits one quad per silhouette edge (measured 2.31-2.43 quads per wing, matching the n/2 expectation for the observed 4/5/6-gon mix), all in one flat colour under a single layer alpha. Tree shadows are the tree's own crown polygon translated - the shadow-layer blob histogram is bit-identical to the crown histogram, 314 trees and 314 shadows.

There is ONE global Poisson/blue-noise field per map, not one per green: PoissonPattern.new fires exactly once per generation while fill fires 29-36 times, and warp == validate at a near-constant ~6400 (= 80^2) regardless of how many greens exist. Greens and groves are filled by clipping that shared field.

The non-JavaScript network payloads are a goldmine the JS ban does not touch: six palette files reveal a complete 27-key shared visual schema (including colorWater, cityLights and roadSurface, which Neighbourhood never uses - proof the schema is MFCG's too), grammar.json gives the full name grammar verbatim, and words.txt is the 360-word Markov corpus.

Chrome precise-coverage names compiled-but-never-run functions, which exposes the latent feature set: buildSquare/buildRound/createRings/createCenter/createBlocks (more hood templates), drawCone, longStroke/attackDecay0, loadPalette/getPalette, and the toggle list setRoads/toggleGreens/toggleTrees/togglePins/toggleChimneys/toggleShadows - which is exactly the layer decomposition the draw record independently shows.

Only ~110 of 282 executed com.watabou symbols are Neighbourhood-specific. geom, geom.polygons, utils, coogee, tracery and nlp form a generator-agnostic library carrying visibly dead code (PolyCut.peel, Color.lerpHSV, GraphicsExtender.dashedPolyline, 6 of 8 UI dialog methods) - architecture a re-implementer should mirror as kernel / presentation / per-generator model.

Rasterisation costs more than generation: Context3DShape.render is 73.3 ms against 47.1 ms for the entire model+view build, and openfl.geom.Point.new is called 385k-561k times per generation. GeomUtils.intersectLines (140k-213k calls) is the hottest generator routine - a fast allocation-free line-intersection primitive is the performance foundation.

techniques.name: MFCG casing idiom (ink outline = body + 2·hairline)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every ribbon feature (river, road, pier, bridge) is stroked twice: ink at w+2h, then body colour at w, where h is the map's hairline width. Holds exactly on all 7 recorded maps (deltas 0.237/0.242/0.489/0.285/1.112/1.810/1.156 = 2h).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Pier/bridge straddle the nominal width (1.2±h) while roads add (2.0, 2.0+2h) — which convention is canonical.

techniques.name: MFCG map-space scale recovery (h = 0.5/s)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Recorded lineWidths are object-local units. Building hairline h≈0.5/s, so s=0.5/h px per world unit. Pixel-measured: wall 1.9u→8px, road 2.0u→9px, pier 1.081u→4px, river 7.138u→~33px, all at s≈4.15.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether the authored hairline is 0.5px or 1px; the alternative halves the world-unit→metre constant (currently ~3.7 m/unit).

techniques.name: MFCG layer order and per-ward bitmap caching
techniques.algorithm_summary: Display-list order: sea → road casings → road bodies → river+bridges → landmark silhouettes → wards (one cached canvas each, interleaved with piers) → field furrows → walls → towers → grid → scale bar → compass → per-glyph labels → title. Each ward is one texture (344×369 carrying 1076 ops).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether ward grouping is by district or by render-bounds heuristic.

techniques.name: MFCG building shadow (offset ink silhouette under bodies)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per block: all dark polygons first, then all light bodies. Shadow band pixel-measured ≈3px below and ≈1px right of an isolated body (≈(+0.25,+0.7) world units). Visible only where it escapes neighbouring bodies.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Dark fills outnumber light 1.26–1.36:1 and segment multisets don't match a 1:1 offset copy; cause unresolved.

techniques.name: MFCG round joins/caps everywhere
techniques.algorithm_summary: lineJoin round on 4062/4063 strokes, lineCap round on 4026 with butt on 37 (grid, scale bar, furrows). No miter on the map, no dash arrays on any map.
techniques.biggest_unknown: None.

techniques.name: MFCG field furrow hatching (sub-pixel hairlines)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Parallel #a59f93 hairlines at the same h as building outlines, ~9–10px pitch, per-field angle, no field boundary stroke. Sub-pixel diagonal AA breaks them into dots; at low zoom they read as a stipple.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How the per-field angle and pitch are chosen.

techniques.name: MFCG screen-space furniture (grid, scale bar, compass)
techniques.algorithm_summary: Grid 1px #a09a90 (0.267px of ink at s=1), pitch measured 112.4px (=100m) and 120px (=500m/1km). Scale bar: baseline + 5 ticks, majors at 0/100/200, old-style figures, unit switches m→km. Compass: 8 rays split ink/paper half, hairline ring, 'N' above.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether grid pitch is snapped to a round ground distance nearest ~112px or driven by the zoom step.

techniques.name: MFCG curved per-glyph district labels with halo
techniques.algorithm_summary: One fillText per character at 27px IM FELL Great Primer Roman, rotated to a curved baseline, wide letter-spacing, paper-coloured halo ~2px. Per-label glyph canvases 15–55px tall, so label scale ∝ district size.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Halo mechanism — no strokeText is recorded, so it is an OpenFL bitmap filter with unknown parameters.

techniques.name: VG water depth banding, W·(i/N)^1.5
techniques.algorithm_summary: Fill #4c8699, then 3 shoreline strokes at widths W, 0.54433W, 0.19245W in #508c9d, #5592a1, #5a99a6. Ratios equal (2/3)^1.5 and (1/3)^1.5 to 5 decimals on three independent maps; lightest band at the shore.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether N is always 3 and how W is chosen from river/lake size.

techniques.name: VG flat single-pass shadow layer
techniques.algorithm_summary: 453–780 shadow shapes for all buildings, trees and fields drawn in one flat #9699ae pass before the objects, offset down-right ~15–20% of object size. Overlapping shadows never double-darken.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Compositing mode and blur — globalAlpha/globalCompositeOperation are not recorded.

techniques.name: VG gradient-filled lobed tree canopies
techniques.algorithm_summary: Canopy = lobed 'cloud' polygon (14–20 convex bumps), filled with a linear gradient (light upper-left → dark lower-right), heavy dark-green outline at lw1, a few interior arcs. 347 trees × exactly 2 createLinearGradient calls. No arc() — canopies are polygons.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Lobe count/radius distribution and how clusters are packed.

techniques.name: VG embossed terrain contour texture
techniques.algorithm_summary: 2037–3300 strokes of exactly 3 segments at lw0.5, alternating light #a0b78d and dark #687f64 — each dash drawn twice with ~1px offset to give an engraved look. Reads as dashed contour curves in the grass.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What field the contours follow (elevation vs distance transform) and dash spacing rule.

techniques.name: VG two-tone gabled roofs with plank dashes
techniques.algorithm_summary: Per building: light roof half + dark half (≈0.78× light) meeting at a ridge, N short plank dashes at lw0.5 in a near-black derived from the roof colour, ~2px outline, plus a chimney rectangle. Two material families: warm tans and blue-grey slates.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Rule for choosing slate vs thatch and the plank count/placement.

techniques.name: VG road halo + core, and green-cased tracks
techniques.algorithm_summary: Main roads: stroke rgba(197,190,172,0.5) at lw16 then #c5beac at lw8 — a translucent soft edge under a solid core. Minor tracks: fill+stroke #728d67 at lw4 then #c5beac at lw2, i.e. a dark-green casing rather than ink.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether more road classes exist at other settlement sizes.

techniques.name: VG vignette and settlement light mask
techniques.algorithm_summary: Two radial-gradient fills over the 1101×1101 square darken the corners. In 05-37-29 a #ffffff lw24 stroke over the road graph is rendered offscreen and drawn back, producing the bright halo around the village core.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Blur radius and compositing of the white mask; the 128×128 procedural texture's role.

techniques.name: NG roof hatching as tapered triangles
techniques.algorithm_summary: ~80% of all fills in an NG map are 3-segment #222222 triangles (5150–23295 per map) acting as tapered hatch ticks running ridge→eave over the light roof plane, on top of a light/dark roof-plane pair (dark ≈0.79× light).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Tick count/length rule per roof and why triangles rather than strokes.

techniques.name: NG streets as single per-street stripes
techniques.algorithm_summary: One #a69e92 stroke per street, square caps, each street its own width (4.55–6.95px in one map, 6.35–11.56 in a denser one). No casing. The stripe is narrower than the cream gap between building rows, so the road reads as a marking inside the corridor.
techniques.biggest_unknown: How per-street width is sampled, and the meaning of the extra ~11px class in the 05-38-59 maps.

techniques.name: NG three-ink palette and flat layering
techniques.algorithm_summary: Exactly three strokeStyles in every map: #7a8499 (shadow pass), #222222 (ink), #a69e92 (streets). Order: ground #ccc4b7 → green patches #a5a584 → plazas → streets → shadow pass → buildings → markers → per-tree canvases → title (72px Voltaire, no halo).
techniques.biggest_unknown: Shadow compositing mode (#7a8499 resolves to ≈#a19e9a over the ground, which is neither clean multiply nor a single alpha).

techniques.name: NG per-tree offscreen canvases
techniques.algorithm_summary: Each tree gets its own 34×34–64×64 canvas and exactly 6 ops: dark-green fill, light-green fill offset up-left, 3 strokes at lw1 and 1 at lw0.6, with 143–291-segment scalloped outlines. Greens jittered per tree, light ≈1.10× dark.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether the per-tree canvas is a deliberate cache or an artefact of the framework.

techniques.name: FTG three.js merged-geometry renderer
techniques.algorithm_summary: CPU-profile symbols show mergeGeometries/mergeAttributes, buildingBufferToGeometry, computeVertexNormals, getColorArrayForThreeColor, three-mesh-bvh partition/computeTriangleBounds, and troika warmUpSDFCanvas: merged BufferGeometry per layer with per-vertex colour, a BVH for per-building picking, and SDF text.

techniques.name: FTG tiled terrain textures + normal-mapped lighting
techniques.algorithm_summary: 17 captured PNG assets: 64² land-use tiles (grass, wheat, grain, tilled, flax, cotton, pig, sheep, snow, lawn, forest), 128² pebble_beach and cliff, 1024² parchment, normal maps sphere_normal (trees) and tall_stone_normal (buildings/walls), alpha masks edges_alpha and circle_alpha, and a 256×16 colour-ramp LUT (matrix-green).
techniques.biggest_unknown: How matrix-green, edges_alpha and circle_alpha are sampled; light direction and intensity.

techniques.name: FTG hedgerow field boundaries
techniques.algorithm_summary: Every field boundary carries a dense row of small tree blobs along it plus a thin boundary line; farm lanes are thin double lines. This is FTG's most distinctive countryside texture.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Blob spacing/size distribution and whether hedgerows are per-edge geometry or instanced sprites.

techniques.name: FTG map palette and chrome
techniques.algorithm_summary: Sea #67819c, shallow #7a99b8, streets #c6c2bb/#bcb8b2, town verge #adb69d, grass #98ad81/#a5c58f, ploughed #a08d7f, roofs brown→grey by building type. UI CSS variables: --background #f5f3e5/#1A1919, --font-colour #0B0F3C/#f5f3e5, --primary-action #cb3a46/#EC5F66; fonts Cinzel + Noto Sans JP.

techniques.name: FTG labels, plaque and scale bar
techniques.algorithm_summary: District labels: transitional serif, mixed case, thick cream halo plus a subtle drop shadow, curved baseline, scaled to district size (SDF text so outline is a shader parameter). Town plaque top-left in Cinzel small caps. Zoom-dependent scale bar (500m/250m/100m) bottom-right with a unit toggle. No compass, no drawn grid.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Label placement/collision algorithm and the exact serif family.

top_insights: MFCG's whole line vocabulary reduces to one rule: every ribbon is stroked twice, ink at w+2h then body colour at w, where h is the map's hairline; the same h is the building outline width and equals 0.5/s, which lets you recover the map's world→pixel scale directly from any draw record.

VG's water shading follows an exact law: three shore-parallel strokes at W, 0.54433W, 0.19245W = W·(2/3)^1.5 and W·(1/3)^1.5, lightest at the shore, over a dark fill — verified to five decimals on three independent maps.

All three canvas2D generators use a single flat-colour shadow pass drawn before the objects (MFCG ink, VG #9699ae, NG #7a8499), which is why shadows never double-darken and why they are visible only where later layers fail to cover them.

MFCG caches per ward, not per building: 46,000 fills become ~600 GPU texture uploads because an entire ward rasterises to one canvas; NG's opposite choice (one canvas per tree) costs it up to 528 uploads for a far simpler map.

FTG is not a painter at all — it is a three.js scene with merged BufferGeometry, per-vertex colour, tiled land-use textures, normal maps (sphere for trees, tall_stone for buildings) and SDF text, so its shading is real lighting rather than painted highlights.

Round joins and round caps on essentially every stroke (MFCG 4062/4063, VG 100%, NG round joins with square street caps) are most of what makes these maps feel hand-inked; no generator uses dash arrays — dashed textures are emitted as many short segments or produced by sub-pixel antialiasing.

Labels scale with the thing they label in both MFCG and FTG, and MFCG does it by drawing one fillText per character along a curved baseline, with a paper-coloured halo produced by a bitmap filter rather than strokeText.

techniques.name: Shared PoissonPattern sampler (k=50, warped domain)
techniques.algorithm_summary: One com.watabou.geom.PoissonPattern class in MFCG, VG and NG: every step generates exactly 50 candidates, each passed through warp then validate, no early exit, ~0.6 emits per step. validate/step = 50.000 in all 19 recorded runs (MFCG 11500/230, VG 8 runs, NG 7 runs). Consumer is tree scatter (VG Forest via VoronoiPattern.poisson; NG greens/groves via fill). MFCG builds it in a static initialiser with fixed counts; NG builds it lazily on first green (all counts 0 when a hood has no greens). Refutes profile-neighbourhood's 80x80 warped-lattice reading.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Warp function, disc radius, and the early-stop rule (steps are about 1.6x emits, not 2N-1).

techniques.name: VG true stage chronology from CPU-profile timestamps
techniques.algorithm_summary: Order recovered from samples+timeDeltas in 4 cpuprofiles, identical in all: Region.new{createElevation (Perlin + gradient, digRiver->dist2poly inside it) -> createWater (river->setLevel->createDeflection, 50-85 ms) -> createDensity} then Region.roll{buildNetwork (trackers, square, wharf) -> placeBuildings -> spawnFields -> rollForest -> rollName}. Corrects profile-village 4.0 (had water before elevation, forest/fields before buildings) and agrees with the creator's launch description.
techniques.biggest_unknown: What produces the river course/polygon that digRiver measures against before the createWater stage runs.

techniques.name: NG templates = seed geometry + number of sub-areas handed to the generic bisector
techniques.algorithm_summary: From two previously unused captures (large,square,leafy; small,street): Hood.bisectArea = 1 for area, 2 for square and street; Bisector.partition = Normal blocks + bisectArea; detectStraight = makeCut - (Street.new - k) with k = 0/1/3 template-laid streets for area/street/square; square template: Block = Street (plaza consumes a face), Street.extend = 2S-2, buildSquare plaza plus one well and one fountain pin; leafy raises greens to 77% of blocks; cone roofs use 6 longStroke each.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Ring template never recorded; what exactly the k template-laid streets are.

techniques.name: Twisted bisection: stated construction vs OBB inference
techniques.algorithm_summary: Creator (49191011) and FTG author independently (164816716): a cut leaves its start edge at a right angle and meets its end edge at a right angle, with a bend inserted mid-cut when one straight segment cannot do both; recurse until small; discard weird leaves. Recorded makeCut = PointExtender.project 1:1 is the perpendicular-foot step; OBB most plausibly chooses where/which axis and feeds isSmallEnough; detectStraight most plausibly decides whether a straight cut already satisfies both ends. FTG's 2026 fix: shrink the lot first and use the inset ring as blocking edges so splits cannot cross the lot.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Bend position, endpoint-edge choice, stop predicate, width law, reject filter - no source gives constants.

techniques.name: MFCG population constant
techniques.algorithm_summary: Population = buildings x c, displayed rounded to 2 significant figures. Four Settlement-panel readings (286->1800, 856->5200, 3423->21000, 2702->17000) intersect at c in [6.12, 6.13); the 6.29 claimed in mfcg-devlogs-b is refuted by 856->5200.
techniques.biggest_unknown: Whether occupancy varies by ward type; rounding rule assumed round-half-up to 2 s.f.
